author: TGEU
title: 200 trans activists gather in Ljubljana amid growing political backlash against trans rights
content:
Around 200 trans activists from across Europe and Central Asia will gather in Ljubljana this week for the 10th TGEU European and Central Asian Trans Council, taking place from 11–13 September.


Against a backdrop of increasing political attacks on trans rights, democratic backsliding and growing pressure on civil society across the region, the Council will bring together activists to exchange strategies, strengthen cross-border solidarity and shape the future direction of the trans movement in Europe and Central Asia.


“This year’s Council theme, Transphoria, joins resistance and celebration. We resist so that we can live, and we live to celebrate. It is not by accident that our communities are the pillars of the fight for human rights. What at first seems disruptive, how we challenge scarcity, borders and limits, soon becomes undeniable. We keep insisting on what is vital: housing, food, healthcare, work, accessibility, citizenship, and freedom of movement, which are not privileges but preconditions for life of any kind. There is always a tension between wanting to walk away from what hurts us and choosing, again, to stay. And gathering in this capacity says: “We are here to stay.”


– Isa Nico Borrelli (they/them), Chair of the Board, TGEU 


The Council will place trans rights firmly within wider European political debates, including through a session on combating anti-trans legislation and policy featuring Yanna Parnin of the Council of Europe’s SOGIESC Unit and Susanne Knöfel of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Justice and Consumers (DG JUST).


A key discussion,

EU’s neighbourhood as the new battleground: Trans people on the frontlines of the movement for democracy and European integration,

 will bring together perspectives from Montenegro, Ukraine and Türkiye, alongside a Slovenian political perspective.


“Trans rights are increasingly being used as a political battleground across our region. The same forces attacking the human rights of trans people are challenging the rights of all marginalised people, as well as democratic institutions, civil society and the principle that everyone should be able to live with dignity and respect. Governments, institutions and national policymakers have a responsibility to respond to this growing backlash and to ensure that fundamental rights are protected in practice, not only on paper. Bringing trans activists together from across Europe and Central Asia is essential to building the political strategies, alliances and solidarity we need, not only to respond to today’s challenges but to defend and advance trans rights across the region in the years ahead.” 


– Juliane Rosin (she/her), Executive Director, TGEU


Participants will also examine strategic litigation before European and international courts, the implementation of the Common European Asylum System and the experiences of trans asylum seekers and refugees, as well as digital rights, online hate and the impact of emerging technologies.


The Council is being hosted in Ljubljana by TGEU member organisations TransAkcija and Legebitra, bringing the European and Central Asian trans movement together in Slovenia at a time of significant political change across the region.

“We are seeing a growing effort to turn trans people into a political wedge – in Slovenia, across Europe and far beyond. Against that, more than just good policy is necessary. What we need is organised communities, shared knowledge and solidarity across borders. Bringing the TGEU Council to Ljubljana is a chance to strengthen the movement by rooting it in the lived realities of trans people in Slovenia and the wider region.”


– Nuka Horvat (they), Director of TransAkcija Institute


Alongside its political and strategic discussions, the Council will create space for community connection, creativity and celebration. Participants will explore the future of the movement through sessions on non-binary communities, trans sex workers and community-led resistance.


“Hosting TGEU’s Council in Ljubljana is particularly significant at a time when trans communities across Europe are confronting a growing wave of anti-trans politics, institutional hostility, and attempts to roll back our freedoms. Coming together to connect, learn from one another, and reaffirm our claim to a future is an act of collective resilience. And resilience, as queer history has shown at pivotal moments of change, can only be built through community care, radical …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Cupo laboral trans: la Justicia ordena reincorporar a otra trabajadora despedida
content:
Los fallos exigen que el gobierno incorpore a trabajadorxs trans que habían ingresado al Estado por la ley de cupo laboral. Los casos que faltan.


Por Agustina Ramos. Edición: Maby Sosa


La Justicia ordenó la reincorporación de Natasha Narmona a su puesto laboral en el Ministerio de Economía de la Nación. Se trata de la primera mujer trans que ingresó a trabajar en esta cartera a través de la

Ley de Cupo Laboral Travesti Trans

 y

en noviembre del 2025 fue despedida

. El fallo favorable se suma a otros en el mismo sentido. Sin embargo, aún no fue reincorporada. Mientras tanto, otras personas travestis y trans continúan en engorrosos procesos judiciales.


“Esto no es un privilegio, es parte de la defensa de mis derechos y de mi trabajo. Es importante que el Estado no solo habilite el ingreso, sino que garantice la permanencia”, compartió a Presentes Narmona.


La sentencia fue firmada por los jueces Gabriel de Vedia y Enrique Catani de la Sala V de la Cámara Nacional de Apelaciones del Trabajo el 7 de agosto pasado. En ella resolvieron revocar la resolución dictada en primera instancia y hacer lugar a la medida solicitada por Narmona. En este sentido, ordenaron “la reinstalación provisoria de la Sra. Natasha Narmona en su puesto de trabajo en las mismas condiciones en las cuales se encontraba (…) dentro del plazo de cinco días de notificada la sentencia”.


Para la mujer trans despedida se trata de “una victoria colectiva”. Sin embargo, también compartió que el plazo fijado por el Poder Judicial para su reincorporación terminó y no hubo respuesta alguna de parte del Ministerio de Economía.


“El viernes pasado enviamos un telegrama denunciando este incumplimiento e intimando a que lo cumplieran en 24 horas. Pero ese tiempo también pasó y el ministerio no solo no lo hace, sino que tampoco explica por qué no lo hace. Esto es muy grave”, agregó.


Natasha muestra el fallo de la Justicia.


La lucha colectiva y la urgencia particular


El caso tiene una relevancia colectiva: implica la falta de cumplimiento de una ley

(la N° 27.636

) y de una orden judicial por parte de un organismo del Estado Nacional. En este sentido, el caso cuenta con el apoyo de un amicus curiae, una presentación mediante la cual organizaciones y personas con experiencia en una problemática pueden aportar al tribunal argumentos y una perspectiva de derechos. Son parte del amicus las organizaciones

ATTTA

,

ATE

,

Mocha Celis

, el

Movimiento Travesti Trans Argentina

 y referentas del colectivo como Pía Ceballos, Sher Lescano y Alba Rueda.


Desde el despido casi un año atrás, las condiciones de vida de Natasha empeoraron drásticamente. “Mi sueldo era el mínimo. Si bien no me alcanzaba –eran 400 mil pesos– me ayudaba a sostener de alguna manera mi vida. De poder tener un plato de comida, ahora dependo de un comedor que queda acá en Munro (provincia de Buenos Aires). Comemos mi vieja y yo. Yo soy cuidadora de mi mamá que cobra la mínima de la jubilación”.


También impactó en su salud. “Tengo un tratamiento psicoterapéutico y cuando me despidieron perdí la obra social. Hoy la salud pública está en una situación grave y esto me revictimiza. En el momento de mi despido además cursaba una fractura de peroné. Recién me operaron el 29 de julio”.


Natasha ingresó a trabajar al Ministerio de Economía de la Nación en octubre de 2021 bajo el marco de la

Ley de Promoción del Acceso al Empleo Formal para Personas Travestis, Transexuales y Transgénero “Diana Sacayán – Lohana Berkins” (N° 27.636)

. La normativa promulgada en 2021

establece un cupo laboral mínimo del 1% para personas travestis, transexuales y transgénero en la administración pública nacional

.


En contra de la ley


Tanto el suyo como otros despidos en el sector público se dieron en un contexto de discriminación. “La despiden con tutela sindical, estaba de licencia médica y además había ingresado por el cupo laboral trans. Ser despedida en ese contexto se torna discriminatorio tanto por su actividad gremial como por su género. Además de que se encontraba de licencia médica”, explicó a

Presentes

 la abogada de Narmona, Eliana Bagnera, integrante del equipo jurídico de la Asociación de Trabajadores del Estado (ATE) Capital.


Según el último

registro disponible

 (enero de 2025), de les 150 trabajadores TTNB (travesti, trans y no binarie) despedides en el primer año de gestión del gobierno de Javier Milei, 50 fueron reincorporades. Treinta y tres lo hicieron por vía gremial …

author: Lillian Kollross
title: Women’s Tennis Association Introduces Mandatory Sex Testing for All Players
content:
Last month, the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) introduced a new policy requiring all players on the professional tour to undergo genetic sex testing. The one-time test must be negative for the SRY gene, the part of DNA typically found on the Y chromosome and plays a major role in initiating male sexual development.

Players must submit a cheek swab, saliva test, or a blood sample, and sign an agreement acknowledging that refusing the test could result in disciplinary action. The genetic sex test will also be required for players to compete in the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

The WTA is the first major women’s sports organization to run genetic testing on all its players. This policy represents a significant change from their former policy, which was last updated in 2024, that allowed transgender women to play if their testosterone levels were below 2.5 nmol/L for two consecutive years.

There are currently no openly transgender women competing in the WTA Tour. In fact, the sport has only had one openly transgender player, Renee Richards, and she has not competed since 1981.

The WTA wanted to make it clear that there is “no intent to disrespect or question the gender identity or the dignity of any person,” and that their policy distinguishes between a person’s gender identity and their biological sex. However, this new policy adds to the ever-growing debate about transgender athletes competing in women’s sports.

In February 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order banning transgender women from participating in women and girls’ competitive sports. Following the president’s actions, the International Olympic Committee implemented SRY gene testing for the 2028 Olympics, which effectively bans transgender female athletes from competing in the women’s events.

The policy does not only affect transgender women but also cisgender women with high testosterone levels. Testosterone is naturally present in both males and females. What makes us different is how much testosterone we each have. For instance, women with PMOS tend to have higher levels of testosterone than women without the condition.

The policy therefore raises questions beyond transgender participation.What will happen to these women who are born female and identify as female? Would they have to compete with men?

The WTA has stated that players who test positive and have a sex development condition that causes them to have high levels of testosterone—like Complete Androgen Insensitivity Syndrome—will be allowed to play if they prove they never experience “Male Mini-puberty or Male Adolescent Puberty.” Requiring athletes to undergo genetic testing in the first place places women’s bodies under a new level of scrutiny.

Regardless of what the WTA says, this new policy is a solution to a problem that does not exist. As debates over transgender participation in sports continue, the WTA’s new policy demonstrates how efforts to regulate women’s athletics increasingly involve determining who qualifies as a woman in the first place.

title: Communiqué vom revolutionären Block an der Pride Aargau 2026
content:
Am 5. September haben wir uns zusammengetan und einen starken, lauten und sichtbaren revolutionären Block auf die Strassen Aaraus getragen. Wir haben uns den Raum genommen, den wir brauchen, und damit gezeigt: Pride lässt sich nicht auf Konsum und bunte Logos reduzieren. Pride ist politisch und wir haben sie selbstbestimmt politisch gemacht.


Die Geschichte unserer Bewegung beginnt nicht mit Sponsoren, CSD-Bühnen oder Regenbogenwerbung. Sie beginnt mit Widerstand. Stonewall war kein harmloses Fest und kein höflicher Appell an die Mächtigen. Es war ein Aufstand von Menschen, die sich gegen Polizeigewalt, Repression und eine Gesellschaft gewehrt haben, die ihnen keinen Platz zugestehen wollte. Gerade deshalb ist es fatal, wenn heute versucht wird, Pride zu entpolitisieren.


Gleichzeitig erklärt die Leitung der Pride Aargau ihre Demonstration selbst als «explizit politische Aktion für queere Rechte und Anliegen» und fordert queere Fahnen, Plakate und Banner. Wer daraus dennoch ableitet, Politik müsse vor den Toren der Pride Halt machen, widerspricht dem Ursprung und dem Charakter unserer Bewegung.


Wir lassen uns unsere Politik nicht vorgeben.


STONEWALL WAS A RIOT — WE WON'T BE QUIET!


Eine queere Befreiung, die an nationalen Grenzen endet, bleibt unvollständig. Unsere Kämpfe sind miteinander verbunden – mit feministischen Kämpfen, antirassistischem Widerstand und den Kämpfen gegen Kolonialismus, Besatzung und kapitalistische Ausbeutung.


Deshalb haben wir auch dieses Jahr unmissverständlich gesagt:


NO PRIDE IN GENOCIDE!


Während in Gaza Menschen getötet, vertrieben und ihrer Lebensgrundlagen beraubt werden, darf eine Pride nicht so tun, als hätte all das nichts mit unserer politischen Verantwortung zu tun. Für uns ist Solidarität nicht davon abhängig, ob sie bequem ist oder in das Bild einer unpolitischen Feier passt.


Queere Menschen existieren überall. Auch in Palästina kämpfen sie gegen Queerfeindlichkeit und patriarchale Verhältnisse. Ihre Existenz darf nicht dazu benutzt werden, eine ganze Bevölkerung zu entmenschlichen oder Besatzung und staatliche Gewalt zu legitimieren.


Wir weigern uns, Menschen gegeneinander ausspielen zu lassen. Wer Queerfeindlichkeit bekämpft, darf nicht gleichzeitig Rassismus und Islamfeindlichkeit fördern. Wer gegen patriarchale Gewalt einsteht, darf nicht darüber schweigen, wenn Menschen unter Besatzung, Vertreibung und einem Genozid leiden.


Solidarität bedeutet, die Widersprüche auszuhalten und trotzdem gemeinsam gegen Unterdrückung zu kämpfen.


Von Aarau bis Palästina, von der feministischen Bewegung in Rojava bis zu den queeren Kämpfen weltweit: Unsere Kämpfe sind miteinander verbunden.


HOCH DIE INTERNATIONALE SOLIDARITÄT!


Pride hat eine Geschichte des Widerstands gegen die Polizei. Und diese Geschichte ist nicht einfach abgeschlossen.


Auch an unserer Pride waren Repression und Kontrolle präsent. Mehrfach versuchten die Bullen, unseren Demozug zu stoppen. Durch die grosse Masse unseres Blocks, unsere Entschlossenheit und unseren Zusammenhalt konnten sie das nicht durchsetzen.


Das ist für uns kein nebensächlicher Zwischenfall. Eine Institution, die für Ordnung sorgt, setzt immer auch fest, wessen Sicherheit, wessen Freiheit und wessen Interessen geschützt werden. Queere Menschen erleben polizeiliche Kontrolle und Repression nicht unabhängig von Rassismus, Klassenzugehörigkeit, Geschlecht oder Aufenthaltsstatus.


Wir haben deshalb keinen Grund, der Polizei für ihre vermeintliche «Schutzfunktion» dankbar zu sein.


Unsere Befreiung wird nicht von oben verteilt. Sie wird erkämpft – auf der Strasse, in unseren Communities und durch Organisierung.


BOTTOM AND TOPS — WE ALL HATE COPS!


Ein Regenbogen auf einem Firmenlogo verändert keine gesellschaftlichen Verhältnisse.


Während Unternehmen & Parteien Pride als Marketingfläche nutzen, bleiben Ausbeutung, soziale Ungleichheit und Abhängigkeiten bestehen. Unsere Identitäten werden verkauft, unsere Kämpfe zur Marke gemacht und unsere Wut in Konsum verwandelt. Genau darin liegt das Problem des Rainbow Capitalism: Nicht unsere Befreiung steht im Zentrum, sondern die Frage, wie sich mit unserer Existenz Profit machen lässt.


Eine Pride, die sich problemlos vermarkten lässt, stellt für die bestehenden Verhältnisse keine Bedrohung dar.


Eine Pride, die über Sichtbarkeit hinausgeht, schon.


Wir wollen nicht nur akzeptiert werden, solange wir gute Konsumentinnen, Angestellte oder Kundinnen sind. Wir wollen keine …

author: anred
title: El conurbano sur volvió a encontrarse: debate, organización y marcha en Monte Grande
content:
Fotos: Rocío Cisterna


En un contexto de profundización de la crisis económica y social, el sábado se realizó el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur. La jornada reunió a organizaciones y participantes del conurbano sur en una instancia de debate y convivencia. Salud, trabajo, educación, violencias y derechos humanos fueron los ejes de las rondas, que tuvieron una amplia participación. El encuentro finalizó con una marcha por el centro de Monte Grande.

Por ANRed 


Este sábado se llevó adelante el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur, una nueva jornada de participación, intercambio y organización que reunió a organizaciones transfeministas y participantes de distintos territorios del conurbano sur.


A lo largo del encuentro se desarrollaron cinco rondas de debate: Salud, Trabajo, Educación, Violencias y Derechos Humanos. Los espacios tuvieron una importante concurrencia y permitieron compartir experiencias, problemáticas y herramientas a partir de las distintas realidades territoriales.


En la ronda de Salud, una de las participantes destacó el valor del intercambio y de la construcción colectiva: “Estamos muy contentxs por este nuevo encuentro que nos reúne a todes para pensarnos desde el conurbano sur. Participé de la ronda de Salud y fue muy enriquecedor el intercambio que nos dimos para pensar en tejer redes para sostenernos en estos momentos de profundización de las crisis”.


“Es muy importante saber que nos tenemos y que podemos confiar en nuestras organizaciones transfeministas”, agregó.


Además de las rondas, la jornada estuvo atravesada por una gran convivencia entre quienes participaron del encuentro, generando un espacio para compartir experiencias y fortalecer los vínculos entre organizaciones y territorios.


 


Una marcha por Monte Grande


Como cierre de la jornada, se realizó una marcha que comenzó en el Instituto Superior de Formación Docente N°35 y recorrió distintos puntos de Monte Grande.


Una de las primeras paradas fue el Hospital Santamarina, donde las organizaciones feministas denunciaron las presiones ejercidas por grupos antiderechos para impedir que se garantice el acceso a la interrupción voluntaria del embarazo, derecho contemplado por la Ley 27.610 de Acceso a la Interrupción Voluntaria del Embarazo.


La movilización continuó hasta la Comisaría Nro 1, donde se realizó una intervención artística. En la puerta de la dependencia policial fueron arrojadas cajas de pizza con distintas leyendas, entre ellas “Ustedes tienen que cuidarnos”, en referencia a la falta de respuestas frente a las agresiones machistas y las situaciones de violencia que atraviesan mujeres, travestis, lesbianas y personas no binarias.


La marcha continuó por la Municipalidad de Esteban Echeverría y la iglesia, para finalizar en la Plaza de Monte Grande, donde se realizó el cierre de la jornada.


Una de las participantes destacó el significado del encuentro y su dimensión colectiva: “Venir a los encuentros te llena de alegría, que no es poco en estos momentos de individualismo y sufrimiento colectivo. Saber que hay muches en diferentes lugares haciendo lo posible e imposible para mejorar nuestra calidad de vida estimula a salir de la queja y ponernos a trabajar en comunidad”.


“Celebro haber participado de este evento, que es único e importante en el conurbano sur”, agregó.


De esta manera, el 11° Encuentro Regional de Zona Sur combinó debate, intercambio y movilización, fortaleciendo un espacio de articulación entre organizaciones y territorios del conurbano sur..

title: Justice4Nzoy – gemeinsam gegen Rassismus und Polizei!
content:
Samstag, 12. September 2026, 14 Uhr Landesmuseum Zürich: Justice4Nzoy! Demonstration gegen Rassismus, Polizeigewalt und die Aufrüstung der Herrschenden.


Roger Nzoy Wilhelm wurde am 30. August 2021 von einem Polizisten erschossen. Sein Tod ist kein Einzelfall. Bei Polizeieinsätzen allein im Kanton Waadt wurden in den letzten Jahren auch Lamin Fatty, Hervé Mandundu, Mike Ben Peter, Michael Kenechukwu Ekemezie, die 14-jährige Camila und der 17-jährige Marvin getötet.


Rassistische Polizeigewalt hat System: Sie beginnt bei den Polizeischikanen, denen People of Color täglich ausgesetzt sind, und endet immer wieder bei tödlicher Gewalt. Der Kampf für Gerechtigkeit für Nzoy ist deshalb auch ein Kampf gegen alle Formen des staatlichen Rassismus.


Die diesjährige Demonstration steht im Zeichen der Militarisierung. Rassistische Polizeigewalt und die aktuelle Aufrüstung der Herrschenden gehören zusammen. So beruht der Kapitalismus auf der Ausbeutung von Ressourcen und Arbeitskraft – hier und besonders gewaltsam im globalen Süden. Für diese Ausbeutung benötigt er rassistische Gewalt, die von kolonialer Dominanz über die globale Ausbeutung bis zum hochgerüsteten Migrationsregime reicht. Der Genozid in Palästina zeigt aktuell, welche Brutalität die imperialistische Dynamik des Kapitalismus entfesseln kann.


In Europa schreitet die Militarisierung voran. In der kapitalistischen Krise verschärfen sich die gesellschaftlichen Widersprüche und der Staat setzt zur Sicherung seiner Interessen vermehrt auf militärische Gewalt: Kriege gegen aussen und Repression gegen innen. Rassismus ist dabei ein wichtiges Machtmittel. Zur Klassengesellschaft gehören nicht nur die Widersprüche zwischen herrschender und arbeitender Klasse, sondern auch rassistische Spaltungen innerhalb der ausgebeuteten Klasse. People of Color werden systematisch in prekäre Arbeitsverhältnisse gedrängt. Antimuslimischer Rassismus normalisiert den Genozid in Gaza und die Repression gegen die Palästina-Solidarität. Polizeigewalt setzt die Klassenherrschaft durch und wird dabei von rassistischer Ideologie gestützt.


Doch dieser Unterdrückung steht eine reiche Geschichte des Widerstands entgegen. In Europa reicht sie von migrantischem Widerstand an den Grenzen und in den Knästen bis zu Kämpfen gegen Polizeibrutalität wie der Kampagne für Oury Jalloh. In den USA verbinden sich die Erfahrungen der Black Panthers, der Black-Lives-Matter-Bewegung und des Widerstands gegen ICE. In all diesen Kämpfen zeigt sich die zentrale Bedeutung der Community-Arbeit: der Organisierung in den Quartieren und dem Aufbau solidarischer Strukturen. Von diesen Erfahrungen können wir lernen. Das beste Mittel gegen rassistische Gewalt ist Klassenkampf – von unten nach oben! Die Kampagne Justice4Nzoy greift diese Praxis auf, wenn sie sich im Kreis 4 und darüber hinaus vernetzt.


Organisieren wir antirassistische Solidarität in den Quartieren und Betrieben! Wehren wir uns, wenn unsere Angehörigen, Nachbar:innen, Freund:innen und Arbeitskolleg:innen von Polizei und Migrationsämtern bedroht, erniedrigt und angegriffen werden!


Schaffen wir widerständige Quartiere!

author: Politisches Cafe in der K9
title: 50 Jahre Rock against Racism im Rückblick
content:
in der K9, Kinzigstraße 9 (Hinterhaus),


Berlin Friedrichshain, (Nähe U-Bahnhof Samariterstrasse)


Mittwoch, 16.09.2026, 19.30 Uhr


Runde Jahrestage werden ja eigentlich gern zur Identitätsvergewisserung genutzt. Etwas mag es da schon überraschen, dass es im Fall von 50 Jahre Punk, so der Eindruck nicht täuscht, doch eher ruhig geblieben ist. Sicher, auf arte und anderswo wird die für die Subkultur charakteristische rebellische Haltung abgefeiert und die üblichen Verdächtigen verlegen auf die musikalische Dimension fokussierte Erinnerungsliteratur. Blass bleiben hingegen die gesellschaftlichen Kontexte von Punk. Wir laden, mit dem bekannten Hintergrundbild des alten Clash-Promovideos zu ‚White Riot‘ aus dem Jahr 1976 im Hinterkopf, das randalierende Polizisten während des Notting Hill Carnivals im August 1976 zeigt, zu zwei kleinen Ausflügen in die ‚Kulissen‘.


Abend 1: White Riot? ‚Rock against Racism‘ im Rückblick


Who Shot the Sheriff? (Alan Miles, UK 2005, 66‘, OF)


Punk konstituierte sich im Moment einer tiefgreifenden Krise des fordistischen fixes in Großbritannien, in deren Rahmen erstmals in Europa, wenn wir von Italien mal absehen, rassistische und neofaschistische Kräfte wie die National Front bedrohlich an Raum in Politik, aber auch in Popular- und Jugendkultur zu gewinnen schienen. Hiergegen formierte sich ab Herbst 1976 von London ausgehend mit ‚Rock against Racism‘ eine Kampagne, die den Kampf auf dem Feld von Musik und (Jugend)Kultur selbst aufzunehmen trachtete und von Stuart Hall in seinem ersten Thatcherismus-Aufsatz „The Great Moving Right Show“ bereits 1979 als „one of the timeliest and best constructed of cultural interventions, repaying serious and extended analysis“ eingeschätzt wurde.


Alan Miles, im Hauptberuf bei der Londoner Feuerwehr beschäftigt, rekonstruierte die Geschichte der „Rock against Racism“- Kampagne der Jahre 1976/81 rückblickend im Moment ihrer Neuauflage unter dem Motto ‚Love Music Hate Racism‘ (2002) von ihrer Londoner Zentrale aus und mit Fokus auf die musikalische Dimension der Geschichte.


Zwar wurde die Kampagne in der BRD 1979/80 unter dem Motto ‚Rock gegen rechts‘ aufgegriffen, doch entwickelten sich diese Mobilisierungen in andere Richtungen; die wenigen deutschsprachigen Reflexionen zu RaR führen, von einem neueren Aufsatz von Gerd-Rainer Horn mal abgesehen, dementsprechend eher auf Abwege. Werfen wir also einen ersten Blick auf den Film (und vielleicht noch etwas Kleinkram) und schauen, was es mit RAR auf sich hatte, inwieweit die Geschichte noch relevant ist, was vielleicht davon gelernt werden könnte und ob es sich lohnen könnte, die Thematik zu einem späteren Zeitpunkt evt. noch einmal zu vertiefen.


(Beachtet bitte: Film in Englisch ohne Untertitel).

author: Chris Walker
title: Vance Invokes Racist Tropes as GOP Convention Speakers Stoke Fear and Loyalty
content:
“This is what has become the norm in our politics,” one Democratic candidate said in reaction to the GOP event.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The second night of the Republican midterm convention in Dallas, Texas, this week featured racist remarks from speakers and a call for violence against Democrats from an audience member — before concluding with President Donald Trump demanding a loyalty oath from viewers.

At one point, while arguing why voters should back Republicans in the midterms, Vice President JD Vance objected to the GOP being described as racist. While attempting to refute that idea, Vance invoked several racist tropes about immigrants.

“We were tired of being called ‘racist’ for noticing that our country was becoming dirtier, and poor, and less safe, and less prosperous,” Vance said.

Texas Sen. Ted Cruz used his speech to vilify specific Democratic figures, including New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and others.

Cruz complained that Mamdani “wants to seize the means of production,” a reference to his democratic socialist beliefs. Cruz also made bigoted remarks about El-Sayed, baselessly suggesting that El-Sayed’s past comments on his own personal religious views mean that he has an “obligation to Sharia Law.”

During those comments, a member of the audience shouted out that both Mamdani and El-Sayed “should be shot.” Despite brief pauses in his speech affording him the opportunity, Cruz did not object to that person’s calls for political violence.

In an appearance on CNN Thursday evening, El-Sayed condemned the senator’s refusal to rebut those interjections.

“This is what has become the norm in our politics,” El-Sayed said, adding that politicians like Cruz should “learn to disagree agreeably.”

The event concluded with a speech from President Donald Trump, who urged audience members and television viewers to pledge their loyalty to him.

“Please raise your right hand,” Trump said. “I pledge to the greatest president in the history of the United States that loves us so much he can’t even breathe that I will go out with my family, my friends, I will do it any way — I don’t care if I’m registered or not, I’m going to try and cheat like hell…to vote on November 3.”

Trump also issued an existential warning to his followers. “You know what happens if you don’t vote, you go to hell, you know that, okay?” the president said.

The do-or-die commentaries from Republican speakers at their unprecedented midterm convention is perhaps demonstrative of their desperation in the final two months before voters go to the polls. Indeed, polling over the summer has consistently shown that Democrats are likely to win control of the House of Representatives, with the Senate in toss-up status, despite the fact that this year’s races featured contests that, traditionally, have favored Republicans.

According to an aggregate of polling data compiled by FiftyPlusOne, 49.9 percent of voters say they plan to vote for the Democratic option on their ballots, while only 43.5 percent say they will back the Republican choice.

Esta vez el suceso ha escalado de gravedad, habiendo un

asesinato

. De aquí se lanzó una amplia campaña por redes sociales criminalizando a todos los jóvenes de origen marroquí de la ciudad. La extrema derecha agitó todo lo que pudo hasta que apareció uno de los supuestos perpetradores, que es de origen catalán. Dejando a un lado que se les cayera el argumento, la ultraderecha utiliza estos sucesos de forma habitual y la sociedad va exigiendo medidas "duras", policiales y represivas, antes que luchar contra las causas sociales primeras que originan estas bombas de relojería adolescente. Así pues, el llamdo "Movimento Popular de Manresa" se movilizó y presentó su propuesta, que os la copiamos aquí debajo: 


El orginal, en catalán

. 


Desde A l'aguait, proceso popular de seguridad comunitaria en Manresa y desde el Movimiento Popular de la ciudad,

asumimos nuestra responsabilidad

, como colectivos que trabajamos de forma comunitaria en la ciudad,

de aportar análisis y propuestas útiles

, que nos permitan pasar de la legítima indignación y la tristeza a trabajar por una ciudad

sin violencias, discriminaciones ni desigualdad

.


Estas políticas públicas y comunitarias, divididas en tres fases, surgen del trabajo que llevamos a cabo desde hace más de una década en las calles de Manresa, y del apoyo y las conversaciones con educadoras y expertas en ámbitos como la intervención con jóvenes, la educación y el trabajo social, las drogodependencias, la salud mental y la justicia restaurativa o la violencia juvenil. Están también basadas en la evidencia criminológica y en aprendizajes recogidos en todo el mundo a la hora de combatir la violencia interpersonal, social y comunitaria, especialmente entre jóvenes y desde los jóvenes.


Como Movimiento Popular,

nos preocupa el aumento de las violencias sociales, de los discursos de odio y de la deshumanización en los últimos años

, que sin duda están generando consecuencias materiales, en forma de más exclusión, una peor convivencia y un aumento del miedo entre la ciudadanía.

Un miedo que puede afectar a cómo las manresanas ocupan el espacio público

 y, por tanto, a la cohesión social, y dar alas a aquellos que se aprovechan y arañan votos deformando y distorsionando la realidad para hacernos maleables.

 En Manresa hay violencias que debemos combatir y transformar, aunque sea una ciudad segura.

Del mismo modo que confrontamos la violencia institucional, tampoco podemos ni queremos aceptar que haya personas que son víctimas directas de violencias en nuestra ciudad.


Es necesario, pues, poder

pensar serenamente qué está pasando

, cuál es el alcance de la problemática, cuáles son sus causas y, por tanto, todas las dimensiones que hay que abordar

para prevenir y trabajar en posibles soluciones

. Si algo queda claro, y solo hay que ver lo que ha pasado en otros momentos y contextos, es que abordar la violencia social y comunitaria como una problemática únicamente de seguridad, clamando ciegamente por endurecer uno de los códigos penales más duros de Europa, ni es útil ni ha sido una solución para reducir estas violencias, que tienen múltiples causas.


En el centro, tienen que haber políticas que rompan con las viejas recetas de siempre, que no han sido útiles para disipar la sensación de miedo. title: Uygur: We are prepared to bear our pain for peace
content:
Families who were unable for years to commemorate their children and siblings lost in the Kurdish Freedom Struggle because of intense state repression are now remembering them at condolence gatherings held across Kurdistan and Turkey. At commemorations organised in Istanbul under the leadership of the Association for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture for Families Who Lost Relatives in the Cradle of Civilisations (MEBYA-DER), the tears shed and laments sung by mothers are as heartbreaking as the life stories left behind by the guerrillas. At a condolence gathering in Gülsuyu, Maltepe, photographs of three siblings from the Uygur family stood side by side. Ali Uygur spoke to ANF about his siblings Yaşar, Yadigar and Abdulkadir Uygur, who were martyred at different times and in different places.


He could not accept the racist abuse and torture during an ID check


Ali Uygur said his older brother Yaşar was the first member of the family to join the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Explaining that the family comes from the village of Barman in Savur (Stewrê), Mardin (Mêrdîn), Uygur said: “Our family first became acquainted with the movement through my brother. After finishing high school, he was preparing to study mechanical engineering, but financial difficulties forced him to go to Istanbul to work. During an identity check there, police officers saw that he was registered in Mardin and subjected him to racist insults and torture. Unable to accept this racist attack, my brother joined the movement in 1991. He was only 19 at the time. He crossed from the Serhed region into Xakurkê. His achievements within the guerrilla forces led to him becoming a platoon commander. In 1997, during a withdrawal in Xakurkê, an operation was launched in the area where they were positioned. That day, he and 24 comrades held Lêlikan Hill, a strategic position, until the guerrilla force had withdrawn. They were eventually ordered to withdraw as well. To save his 24 comrades during the retreat, my brother stayed behind until the very end and found himself alone, surrounded by KDP peshmerga forces and Turkish soldiers. He fought there until his last bullet and, rather than be captured alive, detonated the explosive he was carrying and was martyred.”


My sister Yadigar was either tortured to death or died from blood loss


Uygur said that after his brother Yaşar, his sister Yadigar became a target of the state: “In 1994, comrade Şoreş was followed while coming to our home in Mardin, and special operations forces and plainclothes police raided the house. I was six years old at the time. Şoreş resisted during the raid and was martyred there, while my sister was wounded. Uygur said: “The special operations officers stripped her naked, wrapped her in a blanket that had been bought for her dowry and put her in an armoured vehicle. My sister was alive when they put her inside because her hand was moving. But we were later informed that she had died. She was either tortured to death or died from blood loss. I believe the plainclothes officers who came to the house with the special operations forces were members of the Gendarmerie Intelligence and Counter-Terrorism (JITEM), because the same team had previously raided homes in Kızıltepe, Mardin, and devastated families like ours.”


They buried her with comrade Şoreş without performing any religious rites


Uygur said: “At first, we could not locate my sister’s grave. We later learned that she had been buried together with her comrade Şoreş in the cemetery where Mehmet Sincar, the murdered Mardin MP for the Democracy Party (DEP), was buried, without any religious rites being performed. They dug the ground with an excavator and placed both of them in the same grave. They are still buried together in that cemetery.”


My 14-year-old brother Kadir was tortured for two months, my mother gave birth in custody


Uygur said that on the day his wounded sister was taken away in an armoured vehicle, his brother Abdülkadir, who was only 14 at the time, and his pregnant mother were also detained and subjected to torture. He noted that his younger sister was born while their mother was in custody. His mother was released after giving birth, while his brother Kadir Uygur, still a child, was subjected to severe torture. author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: The White Supremacist Pastor in Jake Lang’s Shadow
content:
Minneapolis, MN — On

Aug. 22

, far-right provocateur Edward Jacob “Jake” Lang arrived in front of Minneapolis City Hall in the bed of a black Honda Ridgeline followed by a white SUV occupied by private security guards Lang hired for display.


Lang, who was accompanied by six others in the back of the truck, was here for his “N-word march” – spelled out in whole on the event’s flyer – protesting against the verdict reached weeks earlier against Rochester resident Shiloh Hendrix for calling an 8-year-old boy the slur at a playground last year.


As the crowd of counter-protesters surrounded the truck to drown out whatever Lang planned on shouting into his megaphone, a man in a camouflage balaclava and sunglasses whipped out his phone and began recording. Moments later, a man dressed as Spider-Man climbed over the cab of the truck and lunged at Lang, striking him several times in the face.


Matthew Oduguwa,

one of Lang’s security guards

, was busy pepper spraying peaceful protesters and press when he noticed this, turning back to the truck to grab at Spider-Man, wrenching him off of Lang and dragging him over the top of the balaclava-wearing man, who fell overboard head-first onto the sidewalk below.


Joel Tenney, wearing a camouflage balaclava, falling off of the truck beneath the counter-protester dressed as Spider-Man.


The man, whose real identity was pastor Joel Tenney of Tiffin, Iowa, quickly scurried away through the cloud of noxious chemicals that Oduguwa and another security guard named Steve Major hosed the crowd down with, disappearing somewhere behind the white SUV.


“Bear spray hits different,” Tenney posted to his Instagram story later with a selfie across the street from City Hall, the balaclava peeled back to reveal ruby-red skin and a stream of snot running from his nose, coating his upper-lip. “At least I took down gay spiderman when he started throwing hands at Jake, busted my nose throwing him to the concrete tho [

sic

].”


The post from Joel Tenney’s Instagram story, where he goes by “honorablecrusader” (Instagram).


Tenney, who runs Alpha Pneuma Ministries, was not among the seven people arrested by police later in the day, apparently not accompanying Lang and the others as they fled the scene. 


Hennepin County at first charged the seven with probable cause riot, only to renege on the charges after it was revealed that the n-word march was coordinated with the Minneapolis Police Department in advance – something that was very obvious to those at the scene watching the police work hand in hand with the hired security. 


After a few days over the weekend and 36 hours of probable cause hold, the jail released all but Lang, who was awaiting extradition to Texas after the arrest violated his bond in the Lone Star State. Like the initial charges, that fell through as well, and Lang was ultimately released with zero consequences.


Photos of Joel Tenney with Donald Trump (left) and JD Vance (right). In the photo with JD Vance, Tenney is photographed wearing a hat representing his role as a caucus captain in Iowa (Instagram).


Of all of the men who accompanied Lang on his racial slur-themed event, Tenney has one of the largest national profiles. Like Lang, the Armenia-obsessed MAGA pastor from Iowa is an unabashed white supremacist – a term Tenney cloaks with euphemisms – and dedicates much of his public activism to transforming the United States into a Christian theocracy.


In the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, in December 2023, Tenney led an Iowa Trump rally in prayer as an official speaker. Before praying over the ravenous multitude, he made the case that re-electing “President Trump for the third time” would result in punishment for people who promote “evil” in the country.


“This election is part of a spiritual battle,” Tenney said. “There are demonic forces at play. But judgement is coming.”


This is not such an extreme jump for Tenney, who has directly compared Trump to Jesus Christ in the past by referring to the president as “God’s anointed man.”

author: Kimberly Mabaso
title: Papers, Please: Canon Collins 2026 Essay Shortlisted Finalist
content:
This piece was a shortlisted finalist for the

Canon Collins 2026 essay competition

. The annual competition invites essays that demonstrate thought leadership and offer fresh perspectives on issues affecting southern Africa.


Some of my earliest memories are not of places but of words.


One of those words was

kwerekwere

.


I heard it long before I understood it. It drifted through school corridors and playground conversations, sometimes wrapped in laughter, sometimes sharpened into an insult. As a child, I knew nothing about immigration policies, borders or xenophobia. I only knew that whenever the word was directed at me, it carried a message that was impossible to misunderstand, it said to me “you are not one of us”.


I was two years old when my family moved from Zimbabwe to South Africa. South Africa is where I learned to read and write, where I made friends, where I attended school and imagined a future for myself. It is the country whose streets, accents and seasons shaped my understanding of the world. It is, for all practical purposes, home. Yet there were moments growing up when none of that seemed to matter as much as the place printed on a birth certificate. The older I became, the more I realised that borders do not always exist where we think they do. We imagine borders as fences, checkpoints and lines drawn across maps, but the most enduring borders are often invisible. They appear in conversations. They reveal themselves in assumptions. They emerge when someone asks where you are really from, as though your first answer could not possibly be enough. They surface whenever a person is reduced to their nationality before they are recognised as a human being.


My earliest encounter with this reality came when I was six years old. Xenophobic violence had erupted in parts of South Africa. Years later, newspapers would describe the attacks in terms of immigration, politics and public unrest. My memory is much simpler. I remember sleeping at the beach with my family because it felt safer than sleeping at home. I remember the uneasiness of the adults around me and the strange awareness that something had changed, even if I could not yet understand what it was. Children rarely understand the reasons behind fear, they simply absorb it. Looking back, what unsettles me most is not the violence itself but the ideas that made it possible. Violence does not begin with burning shops or broken windows. By the time those things happen, something deeper has already taken root. It begins in the stories people tell about who belongs and who does not. It grows whenever human beings are transformed into problems to be solved rather than neighbours to be known.


In recent years, South Africa has once again witnessed a rise in anti-immigrant sentiment. Foreign nationals are routinely blamed for unemployment, crime and failing public services. Faced with complex social and economic challenges, it is often easier to point to visible outsiders than to confront more difficult realities. Yet what I find particularly striking is how little legality seems to matter. Public debates often suggest that the issue is documentation, that hostility is directed only at those who lack the proper papers. Yet lived experience tells a different story. Refugees carrying valid permits, students lawfully enrolled at universities and long-term residents who have spent years contributing to their communities often find themselves subjected to the same suspicion. Recent anti-immigrant campaigns and protests have only reinforced this reality, demonstrating how quickly legal status can become irrelevant once a person is marked as an outsider.  The issue, it seems, is no longer legality. The issue is belonging.


When I was younger, I believed documents had power. Adults treated them as though they did. Passports were carefully stored. Permits were renewed. Birth certificates were tucked away in drawers and folders. Documents opened doors, crossed borders and settled questions. Or so I thought. As I grew older, I realised that documents answer only certain kinds of questions. They can tell people where you were born. They can confirm your legal status. They can prove that you are permitted to be somewhere. What they cannot do is convince someone that you belong. That lesson reveals itself in small moments: a question asked with just enough suspicion to make you uncomfortable, a joke that everyone else laughs at, the pause that follows your …

title: Δυναμικές αντικυβερνητικές διαδηλώσεις ενόψει ΔΕΘ, το Σάββατο 5/9, στις 18.00
content:
Το Σάββατο 5/9 στις 18:00, ενόψει των εγκαινίων της 90ης ΔΕΘ, συνδικάτα, εργατικά σωματεία, φοιτητικοί σύλλογοι, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες από όλη τη χώρα καλούν σε μαζικές συγκεντρώσεις στο κέντρο της πόλης, για να διαδηλώσουν με κεντρικό σύνθημα τους αγώνες για ζωή, ελευθερία και αξιοπρέπεια, ενάντια στον εργασιακό μεσαίωνα, στην κοινωνική – οικονομική εξαθλίωση, τους πολέμους και τις δολοφονικές πολιτικές του καπιταλιστικού συστήματος.


Τα κύρια αιτήματα των κινητοποιήσεων είναι η κατάργηση των αντεργατικών νόμων, η θέσπιση συλλογικών συμβάσεων εργασίας με αξιοπρεπείς μισθούς, το τέλος στον πληθωρισμό, στην ανασφάλεια και στην στεγαστική κρίση, αλλά και η παύση κάθε συμμετοχής του ελληνικού κράτους στη γενοκτονία των παλαιστινίων και στις νέες πολεμικές καμπάνιες και συμφωνίες με το Ισραήλ και το ΝΑΤΟ.


Τα καλέσματα λαμβάνουν χώρα σε τέσσερις διαφορετικές τοποθεσίες στο κέντρο της πόλης: Στην Καμάρα όπου καλούν πρωτοβάθμια σωματεία, ταξικές και φοιτητικές πρωτοβουλίες, οργανώσεις και συλλογικότητες. Στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου καλούν οι ΓΣΕΕ, ΑΔΕΔΥ και το Εργατοϋπαλληλικό Κέντρο Θεσσαλονίκης. Στην πλατεία ΧΑΝΘ (17.30) το ΠΑΜΕ. Στην Εγνατία και Αγία Σοφία η ΟΚΔΕ.


Παράλληλα σωματεία και εργατικές πρωτοβουλίες οργανώνουν μετακινήσεις από διάφορα σημεία της χώρας με λεωφορεία, με σκοπό την διευκόλυνση στη μεταφορά των διαδηλωτών στη Θεσσαλονίκη ενόψει των κινητοποιήσεων. Παρακάτω ακολουθούν τα ραντεβού των μετακινήσεων ανά πόλη και αναλυτικά τα καλέσματα των διαδηλώσεων.

title: İHD 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu: Sandığa darbe, sokağa yumruk
content:
Eylem Nazlıer [email protected]

İnsan Hakları Derneği’nin (İHD) basından ve açık kaynaklardan derlediği bilgilerle hazırladığı 2025 Yılı Hak İhlalleri Raporu, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç geride kalsa da birçok temel alanda insan hakları ihlallerinin tüm ağırlıyla varlığını sürdürdüğünü ortaya koydu. Raporda, “barış ortamını besleyip güçlendirecek yeterli demokratik adımların atılmaması, üstelik her türlü toplumsal tepkiyi yargı kılıcı ve kolluk sopasıyla bastırmayı düstur edinen yönetim anlayışının devam etmesi yine pek çok temel hakkın ihlaline yol açtı” tespitinde bulunuldu.

Rapora göre, 2025 yılında en çok hak ihlali tespit edilen iller sırasıyla İstanbul, Ankara, İzmir, Bursa, Van, Antalya, Diyarbakır, Mersin, Kocaeli ve Şırnak oldu. Nüfusa oranla en sık hak ihlali tespit edilen illerin başını ise Tunceli (Dersim) çekti. Onu sırasıyla Erzincan, Bolu, Kırşehir, Şırnak, Van, Ankara, İstanbul, Elazığ ve Iğdır takip etti.

Rapora göre, yaşam hakkına yönelik ihlaller sonucu en az 2.749 kişi hayatını kaybetti, en az 1.112 kişi yaralandı. Yaşam hakkı ihlallerinde başı iş cinayetleri çekti. 2025 yılında en az 2.105 kişi iş cinayetleri sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Böylece 2016-2015 yılları arasında, 10 yılda iş cinayetleri sonucu ölen kişi sayısı 20.009 kişiye ulaştı. 2025’in ekonomik kriz ve MESEM vb. uygulamalarla çocuk işçiliğinde yaşanan kitleselleşmenin sonuçlarına da dikkat çekilen raporda, 26’sı 14 yaş ve altı, en az 94 çocuğun iş cinayetlerinde hayatını kaybettiği aktarıldı.

Rapora göre, Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan’ın “Aile Yılı” ilan ettiği 2025 yılında, kadınlar ve çocuklar yine erkek şiddetinin hedefi oldular. Her gün en az bir kadın ya da çocuk erkek şiddeti sonucu yaşamını yitirdi. Kadınlar en çok iktidarca konumlandırıldıkları “evde” şiddete maruz kalırken, bu şiddetin faili de yine eski/yeni eşler, partnerler ile baba, kardeş, damat gibi erkek aile fertleriydi.

Raporda, İHD’nin 1991 yılından bu yana yaptığı çalışmalara dayanılarak, Kürt sorununda çatışmalı süreç nedeniyle en az 36.479 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği aktarıldı. İHD’nin verilerine göre, 25 yıllık bu süreçte 27.025 kişinin doğrudan operasyon ve çatışmalarda, 9.454 kişinin ise çatışmalı süreçle bağlantılı diğer saldırı ve yaşam hakkı ihlalleri sonucu hayatını kaybetti.

Rapora 2025 yılında, en az 159 kişi resmi ihmal ve denetimsizlik sonucu hayatını kaybetti. Deprem, sel vb. doğa olayları sonucu en az 1 kişi öldü, en az 180 kişi yaralandı. Bolu’da otel yangınında 34’ü çocuk, toplam 78 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Orman yangınlarında 10 kişi yaşamını yitirdi. Kolluk güçlerine ait araçların karıştığı kazalar sonucu 20’si asker, 7’si mülteci, 1’i çocuk en az 29 kişi yaşamını yitirdi.

Ayrıca, kolluk güçlerinin silah kullanma yetkisini ihlal etmesi sonucu en az 3 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 5 kişi yaralandı.

2025 yılında politik nedenler ya da ırkçı, ayrımcı, fobik saiklerle gerçekleştirilen en az 43 fiziksel ya da silahlı saldırı basına yansıdı. Bu saldırılarla en az 148 kişi doğrudan hedef alınırken, bu saldırılarda en az 15 kişi yaşamını yitirdi, en az 52 kişi yaralandı.

En az 9 gazeteci saldırıya uğradı. Hakan Tosun hayatını kaybetti. Dönemin CHP Genel Bşk. Özgür Özel fiziksel saldırıya uğradı. IŞİD ile ilişkili 2 saldırıda, en az 6 polis ve 6 silahlı örgüt militanı yaşamını yitirdi. En az 5 fobik saldırı tespit edildi. 1 trans kadın öldürüldü. 8 ırkçı saldırıda en az 14 kişi yaralandı. 12 yaşındaki mülteci çocuk evinde uğradığı saldırı sonucu öldürüldü. Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı saldırıya uğradı.

2025 yılında en az 1842 kişi işkence ve diğer kötü muamele niteliğindeki uygulamalara maruz kaldı.

Ankara’da gözaltında işkence gördüğü iddia edilen Musa Nargüner, tedavi gördüğü hastanede yaşamını yitirdi. 1’i geri gönderme merkezlerinde en az 90 kişi resmi gözaltı yerlerinde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. 1493’ü toplantı ve gösterilere yönelik kolluk müdahalelerinde olmak üzere, en az 1592 kişi resmi gözaltı yerleri dışında işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz kaldı. En az 185 mahpus hapishanelerde işkence ve kötü muameleye maruz bırakıldı.

2024 yerel seçimlerinden 2025 yılı sonuna kadar 27 belediye başkanı görevden uzaklaştırıldı, 13 belediyeye kayyum atandı. 16 belediye başkanı tutuklandı.

author: Frances Madeson
title: Louisiana Residents Are Resisting Plans to Build ICE Jail on Contaminated Site
content:
Organizers are hard at work to convince officials to roll back an agreement with a private prison operator.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The Alexandria International Airport, which is part of England Airpark in central Louisiana, is currently known as the busiest ICE Air Operations hub for deportations in the United States. Immigration and Custom Enforcement’s Alexandria Staging Facility, a terminus for people being removed from the U.S., is reviled the world over by abused and deported refugees from Cameroon to Haiti. Even as the town’s tourism office works in overdrive to entice visitors to the area’s natural and cultural attractions — the scenic Red River, lush butterfly gardens, and historic homes such as the one where venerated Harlem Renaissance poet Arna Bontemps lived from birth to three years old — violence against immigrants keeps coming.

Last year, Alexandria was mentioned in a lawsuit regarding a child with Stage 4 kidney cancer who was deported along with two siblings in April 2025. Now, the same polarizing federal agency that has killed people on the streets and in its custody is planning to expand its operations in Alexandria. ICE has grabbed another chunk of the England Airpark, which is situated on a former U.S. Air Force base that shuttered in 1992 due to groundwater contaminated with catastrophic levels of PFAS, a class of persistent “forever chemicals” linked to cancer, reproductive harms, and other serious health problems.

If ICE has its way, as soon as the end of September, it aims to place immigrant women (including those who are pregnant), infants, and children, on top of this toxic site in a 528-bed facility, to be housed in a former military barracks. To further sully the atmosphere, ICE has contracted with the LaSalle Family Foundation, an affiliate of the private prison operator LaSalle Corrections, which runs the Irwin Detention Center in Georgia. A congressional investigation found ample evidence of rampant medical abuse at the facility, including medically unnecessary gynecological procedures performed on migrant women.

Louisiana residents are mobilizing in opposition to the immigration jail with the help of CENLA Activism, a grassroots group of concerned residents that mobilizes activists in central Louisiana and organizes mutual aid for communities under siege by ICE.

At the center of this scheme is England Economic and Industrial Development District (EEIDD), an independent political subdivision of the State of Louisiana charged with taking over and redeveloping the England Air Force Base after it was decommissioned.

EEIDD, the governing authority for England Airpark, has a board of commissioners who are all appointed by the mayors of Alexandria and Pineville, the Central Louisiana Regional Chamber of Commerce, and Rapides Parish officials. The 10 commissioners, all men, were persuaded last February to rubber-stamp the contract for the ICE jail. Their executive director Ralph Hennessy told Verite News that “the facilities are set up like a traditional dorm room,” and said to ABC affiliate WBRZ that it would bring an economic benefit to the Airpark.

As Hennessy put it: “There are a lot of people in Central Louisiana that make a living off of the immigration world, the prison world.” ICE will pay EEIDD, the district he works for, $530,000 annually. In May, Hennessy’s own base salary rose from $209,615 to $240,000.

Since learning of EEIDD’s plan to allow ICE to detain children in their community, mothers, grandmothers, Christian clergywomen, and educators organizing with CENLA Activism have showed up to EEIDD board meetings, and they have no intention of letting up. They’ve channeled their fury into demonstrations to raise public awareness in heavily trafficked parts of town on the National Day of Action: ICE Out Visibility Event, and have held prayer services that have often brought participants to tears. Pastor Leah Rachal said at an August 25 service she helped organize: “We might disagree on some of the other minutiae of immigration policy. But not this. Nobody wants children to be detained.”

At an August 27 EEIDD board of commissioners meeting, where more than 100 Louisianans packed the overflow room, Rose Marie Norton greeted board chair Oday Lavergne as “the heart of Alexandria” and reminded him, “The protests aren’t necessarily against you; they’re against the system.”

content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Έκτακτη εκδήλωση & συζήτηση: Κούρδος πολιτικός πρόσφυγας κινδυνεύει με απέλαση πίσω στην Τουρκία


Solidarity with Migrants


ΕΚΤΑΚΤΗ ΕΚΔΗΛΩΣΗ-ΣΥΖΗΤΗΣΗ


Την Πέμπτη 10/9 στις 19:30 στο συλλογικό καφέ (κιόσκι) της Κοινότητας Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών.


Ο Soner Inanç, Κούρδος πολιτικός αγωνιστής για τα εργατικά δικαιώματα και τις δημοκρατικές ελευθερίες διανύει την 16η μέρα απεργίας πείνας σε καθεστώς κράτησης ενώ κινδυνεύει με άμεση απέλαση λόγω της ενδεχόμενης απόρριψης της αίτησής του για άσυλο. O πολιτικός πρόσφυγας Soner Inanç αναγκάστηκε να εγκαταλείψει την Τουρκία καθώς έχει στοχοποιηθεί για τη δράση του από το τουρκικό κράτος και ήδη έχει φυλακιστεί στο παρελθόν για τη συμμετοχή του στο κίνημα του Gezi Park.


Μετά την απορριπτική απόφαση ως προς το αρχικό αίτημα ασύλου του, Soner Inanç κατέθεσε αίτημα ακύρωσης και ακολούθησε όλες τις σχετικές διαδικασίες. Τέλη Ιουλίου, συνελήφθη και βρέθηκε σε καθεστώς διοικητικής κράτησης στο ΑΤ Λαυρίου. Ένα μήνα μετά, μεταφέρθηκε στη Θεσσαλονίκη με σκοπό την απέλαση του. Λίγες μέρες πριν, του γνωστοποιήθηκε καταδίκη στην Τουρκία απλώς και μόνο για τη συμμετοχή του στις διαδηλώσεις του κινήματος για το Gezi Park. Επί τη βάση της καταδικαστικής αυτής απόφασης κατέθεσε μεταγενέστερο αίτημα ασύλου και μπλόκαρε την απέλαση. Αυτήν την στιγμή κρατείται προσωρινά στο κλειστό στρατόπεδο (ΠΡΟΚΕΚΑ) Δράμας. Αν απελαθεί, κινδυνεύει η ζωή του με βασανιστήρια στο καθεστώς των τουρκικών φυλακών.


Ο Soner Inanç από την αρχή της γνωστοποίησης της απέλασης στην Τουρκία ξεκίνησε απεργία πείνας με αίτημα την αναγνώριση πολιτικού ασύλου και την απελευθέρωσή του. Διανύοντας πλέον την 16η ημέρα απεργίας πείνας, η αστυνομία αρνείται να δεχτεί το αίτημα των γιατρών που τον παρακολουθούν να λάβει βιταμίνες, γεγονός που θέτει σε κίνδυνο τη ζωή του άμεσα. Με λίγα λόγια, το ελληνικό κράτος οδηγεί στο θάνατο έναν πολιτικά διωκόμενο πρόσφυγα από το τουρκικό κράτος αρνούμενο μέχρι και τη στοιχειώδη ιατρική υποστήριξη του.


Το μεταγενέστερο αίτημα του κρίθηκε, λανθασμένα, απαράδεκτο σήμερα και θα ασκηθεί προσφυγή.


Ως Solidarity with Migrants, γνωρίσαμε τον Soner στο στρατόπεδο προσφύγων Οινοφύτων όπου πάντα προσπαθούσε με όλα τα δυνατά μέσα να υποστηρίζει τα δικαιώματα όλων των προσφύγων με μια βαθιά διεθνιστική προσήλωση.


Αυτή τη στιγμή η ζωή του Soner κινδυνεύει με ευθύνη του αρμόδιων θεσμών και μηχανισμών του ελληνικού κράτους, καθώς δεν αποδέχονται το στοιχειώδες αίτημα ιατρικής υποστήριξης στην απεργία πείνας και ταυτόχρονα συνεχίζουν να καταστρατηγούν το δικαίωμα του στο πολιτικό άσυλο οδηγώντας σε απέλαση στην Τουρκία για φυλάκιση με άμεσο κίνδυνο για τη ζωή του.


Στηρίζουμε σε όλα τα επίπεδα τον αγώνα για άμεση απελευθέρωση και απόδοση πολιτικού ασύλου.


Αλληλεγγύη στον Soner Inanç!


***


ACİL ÇAĞRILI ETKİNLİK – TARTIŞMA


10 Eylül Perşembe günü saat 19:30’da, İşgal Edilmiş Mülteci Evleri (Prosfygika) kolektif kafesinde (Kioski) buluşuyoruz.


Soner İnanç, işçi hakları ve demokratik özgürlükler için mücadele eden bir Kürt aktivist, gözaltında 16. gününe giren açlık grevini sürdürüyor ve siyasi sığınma başvurusunun reddedilmesi ihtimalinden dolayı halen sınır dışı edilme tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya. Politik mülteci Soner İnanç, faaliyetleri nedeniyle Türk devleti tarafından hedef alındığı için Türkiye’yi terk etmek zorunda kaldı; daha önce de Gezi Parkı direnişine katıldığı için hapiste kalmıştı.


İlk sığınma talebinin reddedilmesinin ardından Soner İnanç, itiraz davası açtı ve ilgili tüm prosedürleri takip etti. O dönemde, Lavrio Emniyet Müdürlüğü’nde idari olarak gözaltında tutuluyordu ve aynı zamanda Türkiye’de Gezi Parkı direnişindeki protestolarına katıldığı için hakkında bir mahkumiyet kararı çıkmıştı. Buna rağmen Yunan polisinin tarafından deport amacıyla Selanik’e nakledildi. Şu anda Drama’daki kapalı askeri kampta (PROKEKA) geçici olarak tutulmaktadır. Sınır dışı edilirse, Türkiye’de işkence ve yeniden tutuklanma tehlikesiyle karşı karşıya kalacaktır.


Soner İnanç, Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edileceğinin bildirilmesinden itibaren, siyasi sığınma hakkının tanınması ve serbest bırakılması talebiyle açlık grevine başladı. Açlık grevinin 16. gününe girerken, polis, onu takip eden doktorların vitamin alması yönündeki talebini reddediyor ve bu durum, onun hayatını doğrudan tehlikeye atıyor. author: Simon Childs
title: Anti-Migrant Protesters Invade Hotel of Pakistani Cricket Team
content:
Protesters banged on the bedroom doors of Portsmouth’s Marriott hotel on Tuesday night, believing they had found a group of migrants to harass. However, they went home after discovering they were protesting a visiting Pakistani cricket team.


Protesters reportedly reached the floor the professional athletes were staying on, believing the four-star hotel was being used to house asylum seekers. 


The chief operating officer of the Pakistan Cricket Board, Sumair Syed, told the BBC the team reported people “knocking on their doors”, but the cricketers “behaved responsibly and didn’t escalate the situation” he said. 


Councillor George Madgwick, the leader of Reform UK in Hampshire was in attendance.


In a since deleted Facebook post he wrote: “A number of concerned local residents spotted what they believed to be migrants going into the Marriott hotel.


“I visited the manager and the hotel explained it was a Pakistani Cricket team staying. The cricket team coach came to speak to me personally and I saw proof (hotel were happy to provide).”


Madgwick claimed he spoke directly to the crowd of “40/50 people” who he said “respectfully accepted” that the guests weren’t asylum seekers and left within five minutes. 


The incident comes as Hampshire Police investigate reports of assaults and criminal damage on Sunday night, when far-right activist ‘Danny Tommo’ led hundreds of people to Portsmouth harbour. The crowd, some of whom were wearing masks, confronted riot police in order to stop the arrival of 120 people who had been travelling to the UK in a single dinghy.


Hampshire Police said no offences were committed on Tuesday, and the crowd dispersed at around 9pm.


Madgwick, who has been conducting an extended media round defending the anti-migrant protest on Sunday night, appeared to take credit. “I’m glad I could do my bit to help the situation and stop tensions rising,” he said on Facebook. 


“The hotel manager was very thankful and actually was sympathetic to the local issues at the moment but just wanted her guests not to have to worry, which is fair enough.”


In a caustic post on Facebook, Portsmouth Stand Up to Racism said Madgwick “fell short of claiming that he deserved the Nobel Peace prize for his mediation skills.”


The group added: “Allowing racists to mobilise like this every time they become suspicious of any group of non-white people in Portsmouth is extremely dangerous. It is racism in action and it has to stop.”


The Portsmouth Marriott hotel has been approached for comment.


This is not the first time migrant-mania has led to confusion. Last year, Reform UK politician Ryan Coogan, shared a picture of some people getting out of a minibus in Cromer and asked, “Is this part of another quiet relocation scheme – although these usually happen in the middle of the night?” The image was also circulated on far-right Facebook groups, but it turned out to be a group of young churchgoers on a trip to the seaside.


Anyone who believes that Reform’s anti-migrant stance could improve things for the workers in the UK might be interested in

The Bureau of Investigative Journalism’s (TBIJ) 

 finding that two of Madgwick’s restaurant businesses have been ordered to pay £4,386 to former employees for breaching employment law, by failing to pay holiday and maternity pay. He told TBIJ the rulings were made without the companies having the opportunity to defend the claims.

author: Unknown
title: İsviçre 5 çocuklu Özgün ailesini de Türkiye'ye geri göndermek istiyor
content:
İsviçre’de yaklaşık 3 yıldır yaşayan Dilan ve Nihat Özgün ile 5 çocuklarının Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edilmesi girişimi üzerine ailenin ülkedeki yakınları ve dayanışma grupları harekete geçti. Ailenin iltica gerekçesinin yeniden değerlendirilmesi ve sınır dışı kararının durdurulması talebiyle imza kampanyası başlatıldı.


Zürih kantonundaki Oberhalden Finkenried geri gönderme merkezinde kalan Özgün ailesinin verdiği bilgiye göre İsviçre’ye sığınmalarının temelinde Türkiye’de karşı karşıya oldukları siyasi kovuşturmalar var. 


Sınır dışı kararının uygulanması için daha önce merkeze çok sayıda polisin görev aldığı bir operasyon düzenlendi. Dilan Özgün’ün kelepçelenerek merkezden çıkarılmak istendiği, ancak merkezde kalanların ve dayanışmaya gelenlerin müdahalesi üzerine sınır dışı işleminin gerçekleştirilemediği bildirildi.


Beş çocuğun yaşamı artık İsviçre’de


Özgün, operasyonun özellikle çocuklar üzerinde ağır etkisi olduğunu söylüyor.


“Bir anne olarak artık korkusuzca uyumak istiyorum; geceleri, çocuklarımı yanımda olmalarına rağmen, defalarca kontrol etmek istemiyorum” diyen Özgün, çocuklarının İsviçre’deki yaşıtları gibi sınır dışı edilme kaygısı taşımadan yaşayabilmesini istiyor.


Ailenin itirazının önemli bir bölümü beş çocuğun İsviçre’de kurdukları yaşama dayanıyor. 


Özgün, çocuklarının ailelerinin siyasi geçmişinden sorumlu tutulamayacağını belirterek, “Geliş sebebimiz ne kadar politik sebeplerden olsa da çocuklarımızın bunda bir payı yoktu. Çünkü onlar çocuk” diyor.


Ailenin aktardığına göre yaklaşık 3 yıldır İsviçre’de yaşayan çocuklar; eğitimlerini burada sürdürüyor, arkadaşlıkları ve sosyal çevreleri burada kuruluyor.


Özgün, çocukların artık Türkiye’de süren okul ve sosyal yaşamları bulunmadığını belirterek şöyle diyor:


“Çocuklarımın burada bir hayatı var. Arkadaşlarıyla, çevreleriyle birlikte mutlular ve yaşamları artık burada. Türkiye’de bir okul hayatları kalmadı. Bu yüzden bu saatten sonra çocuklarım için burada kalma mücadelesini veriyorum.”


Aile için başlatılan kampanyada da İsviçre makamlarından, yalnızca ebeveynlerin iltica dosyasını değil, çocukların ülkede geçirdikleri süreyi, eğitimlerini, sosyal bağlarını ve sınır dışı edilmelerinin çocuklar üzerindeki etkilerini birlikte değerlendirmeleri isteniyor.


Dilan Özgün çağrısını, “Çocukların sınırları ve statüleri olmamalı” sözleriyle dile getiriyor.


Aynı merkezden gönderilen Yalçınkaya Türkiye’de tutuklandı


Özgün ailesinin sınır dışı edilmesine yönelik kaygıları, aynı geri gönderme merkezinde kalan başka bir Türkiyeli sığınmacının başına gelenlerle daha somut bir boyut kazandı.


Bahar Yalçınkaya, beş yaşındaki çocuğu ve İsviçre’de dünyaya gelen 15 aylık bebeğiyle birlikte 5 Ağustos’ta Oberhalden Finkenried merkezinden alınarak Türkiye’ye sınır dışı edildi.


Avukatının Türkiye’de tutuklanma riski bulunduğu yönünde İsviçre makamlarını uyardığı bildirildi. Buna rağmen sınır dışı edilen Yalçınkaya Türkiye’ye girişinin ardından gözaltına alındı ve ertesi gün “örgüt propagandası yapmak” suçlamasıyla tutuklandı. Suçlamaya sosyal medya paylaşımlarının dayanak yapıldığı bildirildi.


Yalçınkaya 15 aylık bebeğiyle birlikte Bakırköy Kadın Kapalı Cezaevi’ne gönderildi. 


İsviçre'nin iade ettiği Bahar Yalçınkaya Türkiye'de tutuklandı, 15 aylık bebeğiyle cezaevinde


6 Ağustos 2026


Olay, İsviçre makamlarının Türkiye’ye gönderilecek kişilerin karşılaşabilecekleri siyasi ve cezai riskleri değerlendirmede başvuru sahiplerinin durumunu gereken ciddiyette değerlendirip değerlendirmediğine  ilişkin tartışmayı büyüttü.


Uluslararası mülteci hukukunun temel ilkelerinden biri olan geri göndermeme (non-refoulement) ilkesi, kişilerin zulüm riskiyle karşılaşabilecekleri yere gönderilmesini yasaklıyor. İsviçre Devlet Göç Sekreterliği de kişilerin iltica başvurusu reddedilmiş olsa bile sınır dışı kararının İsviçre’nin uluslararası yükümlülüklerine, özellikle 1951 Cenevre Mülteci Sözleşmesi’ne uygun olup olmadığının ayrıca incelenmesi gerektiğini belirtiyor. 


Yalçınkaya’nın sınır dışı edildikten hemen sonra tutuklanması, bu risk değerlendirmesinin uygulamada gereğince yerine getirilip getirilmediği sorusunu gündeme taşıdı. 


İsviçre iltica sistemini hızlandırıyor


Özgün ailesinin dosyası aynı zamanda İsviçre’nin iltica politikasında hızlandırma, erken eleme ve geri gönderme mekanizmalarının ağırlığının arttığı bir döneme denk geldi. 


İsviçre’de bugünkü sistemin temeli 2019’da yürürlüğe giren iltica reformuyla atıldı. Başvuruların önemli bir bölümü …

author: Redazione_web
title: Migrazioni, repressione e corsa elettorale. La lezione di Ceuta
content:
La settimana scorsa il governo Meloni ha prolungato di altri 15 giorni la sospensione del trattato di Schengen con lo Stato spagnolo ricevendo, come ovvia contropartita, lo stesso trattamento. Le motivazioni pubbliche e sbandierate sono le solite: contrasto all’immigrazione clandestina, lotta al ‘terrorismo’, ecc. Quelle occulte, per chi le vuole vedere, parlano di rilancio del sovranismo identitario e di tentativo di demolizione di ogni politica immigratoria che non sappia di violenza e sfruttamento intensivo.


La vicenda di Ceuta è stata un’occasione troppo grossa, troppo appetitosa per farsela sfuggire e così; grazie al clima preelettorale già ampiamente arroventato, Meloni e i suoi hanno pensato bene di dar fiato alla grancassa, cercando alleanze a destra e a manca (ognuno ha i volenterosi che si merita) e di mettere sulla graticola il premier Sanchez e il suo governo socialista. Tra i primi a rispondere al loro richiamo la socialdemocratica danese – ovviamente osannata dai ‘giornali’ di Angelucci – e le formazioni dal nazionalismo più becero.


Ma cosa è successo a Ceuta, questo piccolo residuo territoriale (insieme a Melilla) dell’impero coloniale spagnolo in Africa? Il 30 luglio un numero di persone imprecisato ma sicuramente superiore a 60mila, è riuscito a penetrare nella città, soprattutto via mare, credendo che in base ad una sentenza della Corte Suprema spagnola essere a Ceuta equivalesse ad essere in Spagna e quindi nell’Unione europea, potendo così presentare domanda di diritto d’asilo e ottenere una sua valutazione da parte dei tribunali. Ma Ceuta gode di un regime particolare che non contempla l’adesione al trattato di Schengen, poiché non appartiene al territorio metropolitano spagnolo, anche se è sottoposta alle sue leggi e numerose caserme alloggiano nella sua area, come d’altronde a Melilla.


Ancora oggi vi è un rimpallo di responsabilità su chi ha favorito in poche ore questo afflusso ingente in una località che conta abitualmente circa 80mila residenti, creando e vivendo, come si può ben capire, non poche difficoltà.


Inizialmente si è pensato subito alle responsabilità del governo del Marocco – firmatario dei Patti d’Abramo e fedele alleato degli USA – che su istigazione statunitense e israeliana avrebbe operato per mettere in difficoltà Sanchez, allo scopo di punirlo sia per la mancata disponibilità delle basi per l’attacco all’Iran sia per il riconoscimento della Palestina come stato indipendente. Oggi Sanchez scagiona il monarca di Rabat, la sua guardia di frontiera e la sua intelligence da ogni responsabilità e accusa russi, Israele e la destra fascista di avere provocato, con la diffusione a pioggia di fakenews, lo sviluppo di illusioni ed aspettative nelle masse giovanili marocchine e subsahariane desiderose di liberarsi dalle condizioni di repressione, oppressione e sottosviluppo nelle quali sono costrette a vivere sotto il tallone di regimi autocratici, militaristi e patriarcali.


L’operazione, secondo Sanchez, rientra nell’obiettivo congiunto dei suoi attori di sfasciare l’Unione europea, riportandola indietro nel tempo, indebolendola per riconsegnarla agli appetiti delle potenze imperialiste.


Quello che è certo è che l’ondata umana, carica di speranze e di disperazione, nonostante in poco tempo sia stata fortemente ridimensionata con il ritorno in Marocco della maggior parte delle persone, ha fornito agli avvoltoi di turno, ai pennivendoli di regime, a teleMeloni, un’immagine utile alla propaganda più becera fatta di minacce di sostituzione etnica, di barbari alle porte, di terroristi jiadisti e chi più ne ha più ne metta.


Un’immagine prontamente giocata sul tavolo dei rapporti di forza a Bruxelles, cercando di imporre politiche del processo migratorio funzionali alla visione autoritaria e suprematista della destra identitaria. Non è un caso che Sanchez e il suo governo, al netto di tutte le brutture che lo contraddistinguono (vedi la successione di scandali che hanno riguardato membri del governo e della famiglia), sia stato messo al palo proprio per le politiche migratorie messe in atto nel paese, politiche tese alla regolamentazione del ‘mercato del lavoro’ e dei permessi di soggiorno, all’eliminazione del lavoro nero, all’integrazione dei lavoratori e delle lavoratrici immigrate.


Politiche che fanno si che la Spagna sia l’unico paese dell’UE ad avere un tasso di crescita superiore a quello di tutti gli altri. Non che questo sia un dato che ci interessi più di tanto, ma …

.“…“

Beitrag von Christoph Dicke vom 23.01.2026 im BR


 („AfD-Fraktion will Abschiebe-Polizei nach Trumps Vorbild ICE“), siehe mehr Informationen, auch zu Asyl-Plänen in Sachsen-Anhalt:


Nach noAfD-Wahlerfolg in Sachsen-Anhalt: Türkische Gemeinde fordert die Aufhebung der Residenzpflicht von Geflüchteten und Schutzmaßnahmen für Betroffene


Sachsen-Anhalt: Türkische Gemeinde hält Residenzpflicht nach AfD-Sieg für unzumutbar


„

Die Türkische Gemeinde fordert, keine Asylbewerber mehr nach Sachsen-Anhalt zu schicken. Niemand dürfe gezwungen werden, zur Zielscheibe von Rechtsextremen zu werden.


Die Türkische Gemeinde in Deutschland (TGD) hält es nach dem Erfolg der AfD bei der Landtagswahl in Sachsen-Anhalt für unzumutbar, Asylbewerber in das Bundesland zu schicken. »Menschen mit Migrationsgeschichte in Sachsen-Anhalt haben keine Zeit mehr für theoretische Sicherheitsdebatten«, sagte der TGD-Bundesvorsitzende, Gökay Sofuoğlu, der Nachrichtenagentur dpa. Die Politik müsse sie fortan »aktiv vor Rechtsextremisten schützen«. Geflüchtete Personen seien besonders gefährdet. »Wir fordern die Bundesregierung dazu auf, die Residenzpflicht von Geflüchteten aufzuheben«, sagte Sofuoğlu. Niemand sollte an einem Ort bleiben müssen, an dem er oder sie zur Zielscheibe von Rechtsextremisten werden könne. »Wir dürfen nicht erst reagieren, nachdem Menschen getötet wurden«, sagte er.


Aufenthalt nur im Bezirk gestattet


Die sogenannte Residenzpflicht wird im Asylgesetz als »räumliche Beschränkung« bezeichnet. Sie besagt, dass Betroffene während des Asylverfahrens das Gebiet der Stadt oder des Landkreises, in dem sie untergebracht sind, nur mit behördlicher Erlaubnis verlassen dürfen

…“

Agenturmeldung vom 8. September 2026 in der Zeit online


 zu:


Nach AfD-Wahlerfolg in Sachsen-Anhalt: TGD fordert konkrete Schutzgarantien für Betroffene


„

Türkische Gemeinde in Deutschland fordert nach dem Wahlsieg der AfD in Sachsen-Anhalt sofortigen und konsequenten Schutz für alle, die zur Zielscheibe rechtsextremer Gewalt werden


Die vom Verfassungsschutz als gesichert rechtsextremistisch eingestufte AfD ist stärkste Kraft in Sachsen-Anhalt geworden. Für die Türkische Gemeinde in Deutschland (TGD) ist das ein alarmierendes Signal – insbesondere für migrantisch gelesene Menschen, Muslim*innen, Jüdinnen und Juden, queere Menschen sowie weitere Gruppen, die von der extremen Rechten zum Feindbild gemacht werden. Viele Betroffene fragen sich nach diesem Ergebnis, ob sie in Sachsen-Anhalt weiterhin sicher leben und sich frei bewegen können.


„Es geht jetzt nicht um abstrakte Prozentzahlen. Es geht um konkrete Menschen, die sich an diesem Morgen fragen, ob sie auf der Straße noch sicher sind, ob ihre Kinder angstfrei zur Schule kommen und ob sie in diesem Land weiterhin selbstverständlich dazugehören“, erklärt Mehtap Çağlar, Bundesvorsitzende der TGD. „Niemand darf zur Zielscheibe werden, weil ein Mensch migrantisch gelesen wird, einer anderen Religion angehört, queer ist oder nicht in das völkische Weltbild der extremen Rechten passt.“
