author: Unknown
title: Avrupa’da Rusya alarmı: İkinci Dünya Savaşı’nın gölgesinde yeni cepheleşme
content:
Polonya’da askeri teçhizat sergisi ve gerçek mühimmatın kullanıldığı muharebe eğitimi gösterisi düzenlendi

Ukrayna savaşı beşinci yılına yaklaşırken Rusya ile Avrupa ülkeleri arasındaki gerilim, savaş alanının sınırlarını aşarak diplomasi, istihbarat, sabotaj, İHA saldırıları ve askeri hazırlıklar üzerinden yeni bir aşamaya taşınıyor.

Gerilimin son halkası, 4 Ağustos 2026’da Leipzig/Halle Havalimanı’nda ortaya çıkan patlayıcı yüklü İHA oldu. Alman makamlarına göre havalimanında Ukrayna’ya ait bir Antonov nakliye uçağının yakınında patlayıcı taşıyan bir İHA bulundu. İHA etkisiz hale getirildi ve olayda can kaybı yaşanmadı. Leipzig/Halle Havalimanının Ukrayna’ya yönelik lojistik faaliyetlerde kullanılan ve NATO açısından da önem taşıyan bir merkez olması, olayı Almanya açısından kritik hale getirdi.

Alman hükümeti olaydan hemen sonra doğrudan Rusya’yı suçlamadı. Berlin’in açıklaması için yaklaşık bir ay süren soruşturma beklendi. Almanya İçişleri Bakanı Alexander Dobrindt ile Dışişleri Bakanı Johann Wadephul 1 Eylül’de yaptıkları ortak açıklamada, Leipzig’deki saldırı girişiminden Rusya’yı sorumlu tuttuklarını duyurdu. Dobrindt’e göre polis soruşturması, olayın niteliği ve istihbarat bulguları birlikte değerlendirildiğinde Rusya’ya işaret ediyordu.

Wadephul geniş bir çerçeve çizerek Rusya’yı Avrupa’ya karşı “istikrarsızlaştırma, dezenformasyon, tehdit, sabotaj ve saldırganlık” girişimleri yürütmekle suçladı. Wadephul’un dikkat çekici cümlesi ise şu oldu: “Biz savaşta değiliz, ancak her gün hibrit savaşın hedefiyiz.”

Berlin suçlamayla yetinmedi. Alman hükümeti Rusya’ya yönelik bir dizi önlem açıkladı.

Bunların başında, Rusya’nın Bonn Başkonsolosluğu’nun 18 Eylül’de kapatılması, Berlin’deki Rus Evi’nin işletme sözleşmesinin feshedilmesi, Rusya’dan yeni kişilerin AB yaptırım listelerine alınması için girişimde bulunulması, Rus vatandaşlarına yönelik giriş kontrollerinin sıkılaştırılması, Rusya’nın “gölge filosuna” yönelik baskının artırılması geliyor.

Rusya ise Berlin’in suçlamalarını kesin biçimde reddetti. Rusya ayrıca Almanya’nın aldığı kararların iki ülke ilişkilerinde “benzeri görülmemiş bir tırmanış” anlamına geldiğini bildirdi. Rusya Dışişleri Bakanı Sergey Lavrov da, Almanya’nın Rus kurumlarına yönelik kararlarının ardından Rusya’daki Alman kültür kurumlarının kapatılacağını açıkladı. Böylece diplomatik gerilim kültürel alana da taşındı. Moskova’daki Goethe-Institut gibi Alman kültür kurumlarının da kapanma sürecine girmesi bu karşılıklı tasfiyenin bir parçası oldu.

Gerilimin en dikkat çekici aşaması 6 Eylül’de geldi. Rusya Dışişleri Bakanı Lavrov, suçlamaların ve Almanya’nın aldığı önlemlerin “gerçek bir savaşın başlangıcı” anlamına geldiğini söyledi. Lavrov ayrıca Almanya Başbakanı Friedrich Merz’in Almanya’nın askeri kapasitesini güçlendirme politikasını hedef aldı ve Berlin’i yeniden büyük bir askeri güç olma yönünde ilerlemekle suçladı. Almanya’nın Rus diplomatik temsilciliklerini kapatmasını II. Dünya Savaşı öncesindeki gelişmelerle karşılaştırdı. Lavrov, Nazi Almanya’sı ile Sovyetler Birliği arasındaki savaşın başlamasından önce Almanya’nın diplomatik misyonları kapattığını hatırlatarak, bugünkü gelişmelerin tarihsel olarak benzer sinyaller taşıdığını savundu. Lavrov’un söylemi burada yalnızca diplomatik bir eleştiri olmaktan çıkıyor, Nazi Almanya’sı ve II. Dünya Savaşı hafızasını bugünkü Almanya’nın askeri politikalarına karşı bir siyasi silah olarak kullanıyor.

Almanya-Rusya gerilimi yalnızca Berlin ve Moskova arasında yaşanmıyor. Baltık ülkeleri Estonya, Letonya ve Litvanya uzun süredir Rusya ve Belarus sınırlarında savunma altyapısını güçlendiriyor. Üç ülkenin ortak projesi olan “Baltık Savunma Hattı”, Rusya ve Belarus sınırlarında olası bir askeri saldırının ilerlemesini yavaşlatmayı hedefleyen fiziksel engeller ve tahkimatlardan oluşuyor. Estonya Savunma Bakanlığı, projenin sığınaklar, tanksavar hendekleri, “ejderha dişi” olarak bilinen beton engeller, dikenli teller ve diğer tahkimatları kapsadığını açıkladı. Estonya ayrıca savunma hattı kapsamında 600’e kadar manga seviyesinde sığınak planlanıyor.

Letonya da ağustos ayında doğu sınırında VILKATIS adlı yeni bir güvenlik operasyonu başlattı. Letonya Savunma Bakanlığı, operasyonda sınır güvenlik güçlerinin yanı sıra silahlı kuvvetlerin personel ve teknik kapasitesinin artırılacağını, insansız hava araçları, helikopterler ve uçaklar dahil olmak üzere çeşitli araçların kullanılacağını açıkladı. Fiziki sınır tahkimatı, askeri hazırlık, İHA …

author: Jesse Staniforth
title: NAN blames Ottawa for death of Fort Severn First Nations woman
content:
The

Sioux Lookout First Nations Health Authority

 (SLFNHA) and the

Nishnawbe Aski Nation

 (NAN) are demanding “immediate, public accountability” and an independent investigation into the death of Fort Severn First Nation member Miranda Mamakwa.


Mamakwa died on Sept. 8. According to a press release by the SLFNHA and NAN, she had open-heart surgery on April 23 and was supposed to have had follow-up appointments “mandatory for her recovery and survival” on May 28, June 11, July 2 and Aug. 6.


SLFNHA and NAN say in their statement the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits program (NIHB), for First Nations and Inuit to access medical care not available in their communities, failed to arrange travel and accommodations, making it impossible for Mamakwa to reach her appointments and receive treatment.


Fort Severn is located in the extreme north of Ontario on Hudson Bay, near the Manitoba border.


Last weekend, Mamakwa was taken to the Fort Severn First Nation nursing station and transported to Thunder Bay Regional Health Sciences Centre, where on Tuesday her family removed her from life support.


Nearly a month earlier, on Aug. 19, Mamakwa made a

Facebook post listing the four appointments

 she said she had missed because NIHB had failed to arrange travel.


She closed by saying, “If I die, please go after them.”


“Those words,” the statement from SLFNHA and NAN reads, “are now a demand SLFNHA and NAN intend to see answered.”


In their statement, SLFNHA and NAN say they’ve warned for years that delays and bureaucratic failures in the NIHB program were risking the lives of people in Kiiwetinoong and across NAN territory.


“From cancelled medical travel to appointments booked, and missed, with little or no notice,” the statement reads. “Miranda Mamakwa’s death is the clearest and most devastating proof yet that these were not exaggerated warnings.”


The post from Miranda’s Facebook page showing the dates of the medical appointments she missed. Photo: Facebook.


NAN Grand Chief Alvin Fiddler said, “It is outrageous that Miranda’s travel was denied on four separate occasions. There is no doubt in my mind that her life may have been saved if she had been allowed to travel to her appointments. The circumstances around her passing are extremely troubling and the denial of travel by NIHB demands accountability.”


Fiddler argued those in charge of NIHB must understand medical transportation as a matter of life and death, rather than a simple issue of paperwork.


“The officials responsible should be asking themselves why our members are still subject to such a horrific bureaucracy that denies them access to life-saving care,” Fiddler said. “Days before she began her Spirit Journey, Miranda posted to social media that ‘If I die, please go after them.’ We will honour her dying wish by demanding full accountability.”


SLFNHA and NAN are insisting upon an immediate, independent investigation into Mamakwa’s death, including identifying which staff members and decisions prevented Mamakwa’s medical travel.


They’re also demanding a public accounting from Indigenous Services Canada of what went wrong and who was responsible for those circumstances, as well as a direct meeting between NAN/SFLNHA leadership and Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty.


Finally, SLFNHA and NAN say they want to see “concrete, funded fixes to the NIHB medical travel and appointment system for the 33 First Nations SLFNHA serves and the 49 First Nations of NAN before another family loses someone they love.”


“Miranda Mamakwa should still be here today, raising her three children,” said SFLNHA president and CEO Sonia Isaac-Mann. “Her death is not something that simply happened to her, it is the result of a system that failed her, appointment after appointment, for months. SLFNHA and NAN have raised these gaps for years, and we are done accepting apologies with no accountability behind them.”

author: infolibre
title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στη Παλαιστίνη και το Λίβανο – Σάββατο 12/9 19:00 στο σταθμό ΗΣΑΠ (Αθήνα)
content:
Αυτό το καλοκαίρι, ενώ τα κρουαζιερόπλοια πηγαινοέρχονται ανάμεσα στα νησιά και οι τουρίστες κατακλύζουν την πόλη και τις παραλίες, η γενοκτονία στη Γάζα, τη Δυτική Όχθη και τον Λίβανο συνεχίζεται. Οι σιωνιστές και οι υποστηρικτές τους στις ΗΠΑ και την Ευρώπη γνωρίζουν μόνο τη διαρκή επιθετικότητα· επωφελούνται από την επέκταση των θεάτρων πολέμου και έχουν οργανωθεί με σκοπό να συνεχίσουν τις επιθέσεις τους. Αυτό το βλέπουμε πρώτα απ’ όλα στην ίδια τη σιωνιστική οντότητα, όπου ολόκληρη η οικονομία στηρίζεται σε τεχνολογία που έχει αναπτυχθεί για την περαιτέρω αυτοματοποίηση του πολέμου, την παρακολούθηση ολόκληρων πληθυσμών και τη στρατιωτικοποίηση των συνόρων.


Στη Γάζα, αυτή η τεχνολογία χρησιμοποιείται καθημερινά. Από την κατάπαυση του πυρός, έχουν σκοτωθεί πάνω από 1.300 Παλαιστίνιοι, ενώ ο αριθμός των έμμεσων θανάτων από την πείνα, τις ασθένειες και την παρατεταμένη κατοχή είναι σίγουρα πολύ υψηλότερος. Τα τετρακόπτερα πυροβολούν συστηματικά πολίτες που έχουν καταφύγει σε σκηνές, ενώ οι Ισραηλινές Δυνάμεις Κατοχής (IOF) συνεχίζουν να ωθούν την «Κίτρινη Γραμμή» πιο βαθιά μέσα στη Λωρίδα της Γάζας, απειλώντας να πυροβολήσουν όποιον δεν μετακινηθεί μαζί της. Στα σημεία ελέγχου των IOF, τα είδη πρώτης ανάγκης κατασχέονται συστηματικά, με αποτέλεσμα να μην περνάει ούτε καν το πιο βασικό εφόδιο.


Στη Δυτική Όχθη, οι IOF έχουν σκοτώσει πάνω από 70 Παλαιστινίους μόνο φέτος· και έχουν φυλακίσει, με τη βοήθεια της προδοτικής Παλαιστινιακής Αρχής, εκατοντάδες άλλους. Αγόρια πυροβολούνται στους δρόμους της Τζενίν, της Ναμπλούς και της Ραμάλα. Μέσα στις φυλακές της κατοχής, οι φρικτές συνθήκες τεκμηριώνονται και βιντεοσκοπούνται από τους ίδιους τους σιωνιστές, όπως είδαμε πρόσφατα, όταν ο Μπεν Γκβίρ βιντεοσκόπησε τον εαυτό του και άλλους να εισβάλλουν στη γυναικεία φυλακή του Νταμούν. Ο βιασμός και άλλες μορφές βασανιστηρίων είναι συνηθισμένες. Οπλισμένοι έποικοι εισβάλλουν με τη βία σε εδάφη που πιστεύουν ότι τους έχουν υποσχεθεί, σκοτώνοντας Παλαιστινίους, βασανίζοντας και σκοτώνοντας ζώα, και ξεριζώνοντας ελαιόδεντρα, πολλά από τα οποία είναι παλαιότερα από την ίδια τη σιωνιστική οντότητα. Για τη Δυτική Όχθη, τη Γάζα και το Νότιο Λίβανο, δεν υπάρχει άλλο σχέδιο παρά τη πλήρη καταστροφή και τη γενοκτονία. Δεν θα σταματήσουν μέχρι να ισοπεδώσουν τη γη, ώστε να χτίσουν τις πόλεις τους πάνω στους τάφους και τα οστά εκείνων που έχουν σφαγιάσει.


Αυτό δεν πρέπει ποτέ να κανονικοποιηθεί. Δεν μπορούμε να αφήσουμε τον εαυτό μας να μουδιάσει από τη συνεχή γενοκτονία. Η ελπίδα τους είναι να χάσουμε τη θέληση να αγωνιστούμε, να αποφασίσουμε να υποχωρήσουμε στα όρια της δικής μας άνεσης και ασφάλειας, ώστε το σιωνιστικό εγχείρημα να μπορέσει να συνεχίσει το όραμά του. Για τον λόγο αυτό είναι σημαντικό να επαναλάβουμε ότι οι Παλαιστίνιοι, καθώς και οι σύμμαχοί τους σε ολόκληρη τη Δυτική Ασία, δεν είναι απλώς θύματα. Έχουν επιλέξει την αντίσταση επειδή δεν έχουν άλλη επιλογή· κατανοούν αυτό που εμείς στην Ευρώπη και στον Βόρειο Κόσμο δεν χρειάστηκε ποτέ να κατανοήσουμε – ότι η μαχητική αντιπαράθεση με τον ιμπεριαλισμό και την κατοχή είναι αναγκαιότητα.


Από τα χωράφια του Νότιου Λιβάνου, όπου τα μη επανδρωμένα αεροσκάφη της Χεζμπολά έχουν αναγκάσει τους σιωνιστές στρατιώτες να υποχωρήσουν στα καταφύγιά τους, μέχρι τα χωριά της Δυτικής Όχθης, όπου άνθρωποι όπως ο Φαρούκ Αντνάν Αλί Ραμαντάν αντιστέκονται ατρόμητα στις εισβολές των εποίκων στα εδάφη τους, μέχρι τη Γάζα, όπου ο λαός συνεχίζει να αντιστέκεται στην κατοχή και τις πολιτοφυλακές της απλώς επιβιώνοντας και προχωρώντας μπροστά, και μέχρι την Ευρώπη, όπου οι μετανάστες καταπολεμούν τα ρατσιστικά σύνορα και τις θανατηφόρες απωθήσεις – η αντίσταση είναι παντού.


Πριν από λίγες ημέρες, το ελληνικό κράτος υπέγραψε συμφωνία «άμυνας» ύψους 3 δισεκατομμυρίων ευρώ με το σιωνιστικό καθεστώς. Η κυβέρνηση Μητσοτάκη, η οποία προφανώς δεν έχει αρκετό αίμα στα χέρια της, θέλει να μας παρασύρει ακόμη πιο βαθιά στους ατέρμονους πολέμους των Σιωνιστών. Η Ελλάδα θα γίνει – και σε κάποιο βαθμό έχει ήδη γίνει – απλώς μια ακόμη βάση στο γενοκτονικό σχέδιο των Σιωνιστών και του ΝΑΤΟ. Κάθε μέρα που επιτρέπουμε να παραμένουν ανοιχτές αυτές οι βάσεις, που επιτρέπουμε σε αυτή την κυβέρνηση να συνεχίζει τον έρωτά της με τη σιωνιστική οντότητα, που παρακολουθούμε να ισοπεδώνονται σπίτια και να σφαγιάζονται ολόκληρες οικογένειες στο Λίβανο, στη Δυτική Όχθη και στη Γάζα, είναι μια ακόμη χαμένη μέρα. Δεν μπορούμε να αφήσουμε αυτό να γίνει η νέα κανονικότητα.

content:
So kann man sich an einer Liane herumschwingen wie Tarzan.


Man finde eine Würgefeige, die von der Krone eines Baumes herunter auf den Boden gewachsen ist und dort gewurzelt halt.

Den Tarzan-Schwung genießen. 😄

author: Savanna Craig
title: ‘I’m happy I did it’: Ironworker from Kahnawà:ke thinks back on 9/11 clean up in New York
content:
Talcum-like powder covered the ground. Burned debris from the planes and the fallen Twin Towers covered blocks leading towards Ground Zero.


Any noise was muffled by the thick layer of powdered wreckage—not even the sound of your footsteps could be heard.


This is how Mohawk ironworker Lindsay Leborgne described the scenes of Ground Zero days after the Twin Towers struck the World Trade Centre.


“It was hard to believe because I grew up in New York City. I was by the World Trade Centre many times,” Leborgne told APTN News. “But to stand there and then look and there’s this big hole in the sky where two 1,000-foot towers were, it was incredibly strange.”


After the attacks on Sept. 11, 2001, Leborgne drove to Manhattan. Born and raised in Brooklyn but originally from the Mohawk community or Kahnawà:ke, he spent his childhood in New York, continuing into his career conducting iron work on buildings across the city. He comes from generations of ironworkers, with his father having worked on the World Trade Centre.


Days after the Sept. 11 attacks, Leborgne arrived blocks away from Ground Zero, determined to help remove debris and recover survivors from the rubble.


“The closer you got, the more damage and debris was around,” he said. “As you got closer to the site, that’s when you started hearing noise because then they had heavy equipment removing [wreckage].”


Twenty-five years after the attacks happened, he still remembers seeing a thousand or more recovery workers and volunteers crawling around the site, as well as cranes, torches, burning steel, and trucks picking up steel to remove from the site.


‘I know guys that have died,” says Leborne, seen here at Ground Zero. ‘I hope I remain healthy, but you never know.’ Photo: Supplied.


Documents on poisonous air 


This week, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani has released more than 173 thousand documents detailing that the then-municipal leadership knew about the severity of the toxic air quality around ground zero. Citizens and first responders have been fighting for city records to be released since that day.


“Thousands of ironworkers and fire fighters and office workers and so many more, remember September 11th, not just each time we mark the passage of another year, but as Congressman [Jerry] Nadler said, each time they take a struggling breath.”


While 2,753 people died in the towers when the planes struck, or collapsed, 9,400 people have died to health-related causes post 9/11, according to the

World Trade Centre Health Program (WTCHP).


“An estimated 400,000 people were exposed to toxic contaminants, risk of physical injury, and physically and emotionally stressful conditions in the days, weeks, and months following the attacks,” according to the WTCHP. “Responders who worked on the rescue, recovery, and relief efforts reported a range of illnesses soon after the attacks. Survivors who lived, worked, and attended school in Lower Manhattan, some who remained throughout and some who returned to their lives in the disaster area, started reporting illnesses as well.”


Leborgne reflected on the many that risked their health to help recover lives in the days following 9/11.


“I know guys that have died,” he said. “I hope I remain healthy, but you never know.”


Mamdani said that some of the documents released show how asbestos was found nearly everywhere that inspectors tested.


“Those buildings were built in the late ‘60s, early ‘70s, when they still used asbestos and all sorts of things that have been phased out of construction materials over the years, because they found out that it causes cancer,” said Leborgne.


Yet Leborgne has no regrets.


“I’m happy I did it,” he said. “We all felt that we had an obligation. If we can, we can use our expertise to try and help out.”


Read More: 


Mohawk Ironworkers remembered during New York ceremony to mark anniversary of 9-11 attacks


Leborgne has a message for those that were not yet alive or too young to remember 9/11.


“Remember the sacrifice of those guys that went up there,” he said.


He recalled firemen climbing up the second Twin Tower that had not yet been hit, shaking each other’s hands and saying they hope to see each other again.


“It’s almost like some of them knew [that] we could die today, but did it anyway,” said Leborgne. “Remember freedom isn’t free and remember that people sacrifice their lives so that we could live free and we could be saved when you’re in trouble.”

author: Sara Connors
title: Police watchdog investigating incident at Whitehorse shelter
content:
Alberta’s police watchdog is investigating an incident from last month involving a Whitehorse RCMP member at a shelter in downtown Whitehorse.


A news release from

Yukon RCMP

 says the Alberta Serious Incident Response Team (ASIRT) is conducting an external investigation.


According to the release, the officer responded to a report of an “unwanted, intoxicated” woman at the Whitehorse emergency shelter on Aug. 11.


The release doesn’t provide any details of what took place.


APTN News has previously reported that a majority of the people the shelter serves are Indigenous.


The release says that a “third-party” made a report to Yukon RCMP about “the actions of an RCMP member” who responded to the incident.


“A recommendation was made to the Yukon Department of Justice for ASIRT to conduct an independent external investigation. Following the recommendation, the Yukon Department of Justice requested ASIRT to investigate,” the release states.


“The Yukon RCMP is committed to transparency and accountability in the communities it serves. ASIRT will independently investigate the incident and determine the circumstances surrounding it,” it adds.


The territory contracts ASIRT to investigate significant injuries, deaths and allegations of misconduct involving police in the Yukon.

title: Азату Мифтахову в ИК-18 ЯНАО отказали в получении газет и отобрали только что выданные издания
content:
Сегодня, 11 сентября, Азат передал группе поддержки через адвоката, что ему сообщили об изменениях в порядке оформления подписок на печатные издания. Причем сначала ему принесли очередную партию подписных изданий с почты, но после выхода из камеры он обнаружил, что в его отсутствие уже выданную корреспонденцию изъяли.

Ранее в ИК-18, как и во многих учреждениях ФСИН, на заключенного могли оформить подписку третьи лица. Однако теперь администрация ИК ссылается на нормы ПВР, прописывающие порядок оформления подписки заключенным самостоятельно через администрацию ИУ.

Распространяется ли это новое требование на остальных заключенных, или же только на «избранных», группе поддержки пока что неизвестно.

«Азат очень нуждается в поступлении новостей с воли, потому просим вас, по возможности, информировать его о происходящем! Цензура тут относительно адекватная, но, конечно же, проявлять здравый смысл стоит, иначе письма могут не передать» - пишет группа поддержки.

Адрес для писем: Мифтахов Азат Фанисович 1993 г.р., 629420, РФ, Ямало-Ненецкий а.окр, м.о. Приуральский район, пгт Харп, ул Одесская, 19, ФКУ ИК-18. Возможно отправить письмо Почтой России не выходя из дома через сервис ZT.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Over a Quarter of Voters Say They’re Supporters of DSA, Polling Finds
content:
Nearly 6 in 10 Democrats said they back the socialist group.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

More than a quarter of U.S. voters, including the majority of Democrats, identify as supporters of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), new polling finds as left-wing ideology surges in popularity despite the Trump administration’s attempts to quash it.

Quinnipiac University finds that 26 percent of registered voters say they consider themselves supporters of DSA, the largest socialist group in the U.S. This includes 59 percent of Democrats and 22 percent of independents. Only 30 percent of Democrats say they do not consider themselves as such.

The polling further found that the MAGA ideology has more negative sentiment attached to it than democratic socialism. More than half — 51 percent — of voters said that they would be less likely to vote for a candidate who backs MAGA, while 43 percent said the same about a democratic socialist.

Meanwhile, 39 percent of Democrats said they’d be more likely to vote for a candidate who supports democratic socialism, while only 11 percent said they’d be less likely and 43 percent said it made no difference.

This is the latest survey to find that democratic socialism, once considered fringe, is on the rise among the public. CNN found in polling in July that a third of Democrats not only support groups like DSA, but also that they personally identify as a democratic socialist. Polling has historically found, meanwhile, that proposals championed by democratic socialists like Medicare for All are popular among the public.

This election cycle has seen a surge in wins for DSA-aligned candidates. New York DSA-backed candidates and DSA member Florida state Rep. Angie Nixon pulled off stunning upsets in this year’s primary elections.

Just this week in Providence, Rhode Island, democratic socialist David Morales defeated incumbent Mayor Brett Smiley in the Democratic primary. Morales’s campaign focused largely on housing affordability, and delivered him a nearly 5-point win over Smiley, who recently vetoed a rent control ordinance.

The surging popularity of democratic socialists and progressive candidates comes as voters are increasingly dissatisfied with the status quo.

An Economist/YouGov poll also released this week found, for instance, that 64 percent of voters say that the U.S. political system “needs to be completely rebuilt” or requires “major changes.” Only 9 percent said it works fine in its current state.

As establishment Democrats have failed to meaningfully combat the Trump administration, meanwhile, polling last year by Reuters/Ipsos found that 62 percent of Democratic respondents said that the party’s leaders should be replaced, while only 24 percent said they disagreed.

The left-wing rise also comes despite the Trump administration and establishment politicians’ efforts to suppress such sentiment. The Trump administration has taken steps to criminalize left-wing groups and individuals who express anti-capitalist or anti-American sentiment in its wide-ranging campaign to target the left. Many establishment Democrats have been aligned with these causes, working fiercely to suppress left-wing dissent even as it grows within their own caucus.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Documentary on Inuit food, family set to screen in 3 Nunavut communities
content:
Nunavummiut have the chance to see a new documentary about Inuit food, resilience, culture and family this month as

Nirilaurta: Let us Eat

is set to screen in three communities.


The documentary follows the Ugyuk family of Taloyoak as they navigate high grocery prices and the cost of hunting equipment.


Malaya Qaunirq Chapman directed the film, which

premièred

 Aug. 6 at the International First Peoples Festival in Montreal.


It’s scheduled to screen at 6 p.m. on Sept. 15, at Astro Theatre in Iqaluit, followed by a Q&A with Qaunirq Chapman, said Katja De Bock, a spokesperson for the National Film Board of Canada, in an email.


A screening in Rankin Inlet is set for Sept. 19 at 5 p.m. at the community centre. Another screening is scheduled in Baker Lake on Sept. 22 at 7 p.m. at the community hall.


All of the screenings are free.

title: Como Vorcaro usou a imprensa para sua rota de fuga frustrada pela PF
content:
As relações de Daniel Vorcaro com jornalistas tiveram papel importante no seu plano de fuga no dia 17 de novembro do ano passado, frustrado pela Polícia Federal (PF) no aeroporto de Guarulhos quando ele se preparava para embarcar em um jato particular para os Emirados Árabes. É o que se percebe ao analisar a cronologia do dia da prisão, à luz de um

documento

 da PF, liberado pelo ministro André Mendonça por determinação do ministro Edson Fachin.


No dia 17 de novembro de 2025, às 7h41, minutos depois de falar com seu então advogado, Walfrido Warde, ele conversou com o jornalista Diego Escosteguy, do site

O Bastidor

, sobre uma reportagem com informações que ele mesmo teria repassado ao jornalista, segundo os investigadores. Às 11h, recebe de volta o link da matéria publicada e o envia para Warde.


Daniel Vorcaro, do Banco Master, em depoimento à Polícia Federal


A reportagem de Escosteguy menciona um inquérito policial sigiloso contra o Master que corre na 10ª Vara Federal do Distrito Federal (DF), do qual Vorcaro já tinha conhecimento, inclusive do nome do juiz que o presidia, como revelam anotações anteriores no bloco de notas no celular do banqueiro preso. 


Como as informações foram obtidas de forma ilegal ou de informantes que não poderiam aparecer, Vorcaro não tinha como entrar com pedidos na Justiça. Mas, de posse da reportagem, como se fosse a partir dela que tivesse sido informado sobre o inquérito, o advogado de Vorcaro ajuiza uma petição na 10ª Vara, pedindo o conteúdo da investigação e citando como fonte a reportagem publicada pelo

O Bastidor

. 


No início da tarde daquele mesmo dia, às 13h35, Vorcaro recebe um link de Belline Santana, então chefe do Departamento de Supervisão do Banco Central, para participar de uma reunião articulada por ele e por seu chefe adjunto, Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza, com o diretor de Fiscalização do Banco Central, Ailton de Aquino. Desde as 6h34 da manhã, Vorcaro estava em contato com Belline e Paulo Sérgio, que

atuaram

 diversas vezes como seus conselheiros, para driblar os mecanismos de controle e fiscalização.


A reunião termina às 14h10 e depois de rumores que circularam durante a tarde, Vorcaro anunciou às 17h24 que o banco Master teria sido comprado por um consórcio liderado pela Fictor Holding, com um aporte financeiro imediato de R$ 3 bilhões. O consórcio incluiria investidores dos Emirados Árabes e, por isso, ele iria a Dubai para concluir o negócio. Nenhuma comunicação formal da transação havia sido feita ao Banco Central, embora a transação também tivesse sido comunicada por Rafael Góis, um dos sócios da Fictor.


A Fictor não tinha lastro para realizar a operação, tanto é que, três meses depois, entrou com pedido de recuperação judicial, declarando dívidas de R$ 4,3 bilhões, e o próprio Góis é hoje acusado de fraudes bancárias. Mas a notícia, amplamente divulgada, serviria de

“cortina de fumaça”

 para Vorcaro voar para um país sem acordo de extradição judicial com o Brasil e escapar da prisão, se não tivesse sido flagrado no aeroporto pela PF por volta das 22 horas. No dia seguinte, o Banco Central deu início à liquidação do Master. 


O uso da imprensa por Vorcaro se deu principalmente pela dificuldade de checar os acontecimentos na velocidade que o mercado exige — e talvez pela confiança excessiva na fonte; Vorcaro tinha contato com vários jornalistas. No caso de Escosteguy, dono de um pequeno veículo, a PF suspeita que ele tenha participado voluntariamente da trama, já que encontrou uma planilha com o pagamento de R$ 2 milhões em nome do jornalista. A notícia foi publicada pela primeira vez na coluna de Malu Gaspar, em março de 2026, e, desde então, o jornalista

nega

 as acusações. 


Desde 2024, circulavam rumores no mercado sobre a inconsistência dos papéis do Master e, em fevereiro de 2025, o Banco Central já havia barrado a compra do banco pelo Banco de Brasília. Uma situação que exigia cautela, mas que, pelo jeito, foi menor do que o contexto e o personagem exigiam. 


O jornalismo só ganha com o acesso público a informações relevantes para o país; vazamentos e fontes serão quase sempre direcionados ou interessados em divulgar informações. Embora a ação de Fachin, pedindo a Mendonça a retirar do sigilo de parte dos documentos, seja um avanço, para passar a crise do STF a limpo, o ideal seria liberar logo e integralmente tudo o que não prejudicar as investigações sobre os três inquéritos com impacto eleitoral: além do Master, os …

title: Kurds commemorate their martyrs in Serhat region
content:
Commemorative events continue across the cities in Serhat region for those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle at different times and whose deaths were announced in recent days and weeks.


In addition to the families of the martyrs, women, young people, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and large numbers of citizens are taking part in the gatherings.


VAN


The commemoration program organized at the Rado Event Hall in Van under the leadership of the Association for Families Who Lost Their Relatives in the Cradle of Civilizations and for Assistance, Solidarity, Unity and Culture (MEBYA-DER) continues for a second day.


Photographs of the martyrs were placed on tables at the commemoration venue, while banners reading “Em şehîdan bibîr tînin” (We remember the martyrs) and “Şehîd namirin” (The martyrs are immortal), along with posters of Abdullah Öcalan, were displayed.


From the early hours of the morning, people attending the program entered the hall chanting “Şehîd namirin.” Members of the Peace Mothers’ Assembly marched through the commemoration venue, chanting “Şehîd namirin” and “Bijî Serok Apo” (Long live Leader Öcalan).


The program, which has drawn strong participation from women and young people, will conclude tomorrow with a mass commemoration. Those at the condolence gatherings in the districts of Erciş, Özalp and Çaldıran will also join the mass commemoration in Van.


ERCİŞ


The commemoration program organized under the leadership of MEBYA-DER in the Erciş district of Van continues on the second day with strong participation.


Banners reading “Em şehîdên azadiyê bi bîr tînin” (We remember the martyrs of freedom), “Şehîdên me rûmeta me ne” (Our martyrs are our honor), “Şehîd namirin” (Martyrs are immortal), and “Şehîd ronahiya rêya me ne” (Martyrs are the light of our path) were displayed at the Karnaval Event Hall where the gathering is taking place.


ÖZALP


On the second day of the condolence gathering in memory of the martyrs in Özalp district, a commemoration event was held. Attended by thousands of people, the program began with a moment of silence, followed by chants of “Şehîd namirin.”


DEM Party Van Provincial Co-Chair Veysi Dilekçi said that the Kurdish people had reached this point by paying a heavy price and that the legacy left by the martyrs would be carried forward.


Dilekçi said that Öcalan’s presence at the negotiating table in the current resolution process had been made possible by the struggle of the martyrs. “Our martyrs show us a path, and we will continue along that path without stopping,” he said.


Following the speeches, a video presentation was shown. The program concluded with slogans.


ÇALDIRAN


Commemorations were held for the martyrs of the Kurdish freedom struggle in the neighborhoods of Kel, Nezravê Jorê, Nezravê Jêr, Tikme Jerê and Selik in Wan’s Çaldıran district. Representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, along with many residents, attended the commemorations. Photographs of those who lost their lives were displayed, while participants chanted “Şehîd namirin.”


BİTLİS


The commemoration program held at the Gökte Ada Wedding Hall in Bitlis continues on the third day.


Families of the martyrs, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and many residents attended the commemoration. Photographs of the martyrs were placed on tables decorated in yellow, red and green.


The program began with a moment of silence, and “Şehîd namirin” was frequently chanted during visits to the commemoration. The event will conclude following a Mawlid recitation and a video presentation.


MUŞ


The commemoration events organized under the leadership of MEBYA-DER in central Muş and the districts of Varto, Bulanık and Malazgirt continue for a second day.


The events began with a moment of silence for the martyrs. Posters of Abdullah Öcalan and banners reading “Şehîdên me rûmeta me ne” (Our martyrs are our honor) were displayed in the halls. Photographs of the martyrs were placed on tables, and participants laid carnations in front of them.


The commemoration program in Muş will conclude tomorrow with a mass commemoration and a Mawlid ceremony in Malazgirt.

title: Μικροφωνική εκδήλωση για τα 13 χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του Παύλου Φύσσα, το Σάββατο 12/9, στις 12.00, στο Δημαρχείο Περιστερίου
content:
Κάλεσμα από τον

Χιπ Χοπ Καφενέ:


Αντιφασιστικός Σεπτέμβρης – Παύλος Φύσσας παρών.


Μικροφωνική εκδήλωση για τα 13 χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του Παύλου Φύσσα.


Σάββατο 12/09/26 12μμ Πλατεία Δημαρχείου Περιστερίου.


ΓΙΑ ΤΟΝ ΑΝΤΙΦΑΣΙΣΤΙΚΟ ΣΕΠΤΕΜΒΡΗ ΜΑΣ


13 χρόνια από τη δολοφονία του Παύλου Φύσσα 18/9/13 στην περιοχή της Αμφιάλης στο Κερατσίνι και του Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν 17/1/13 στα Άνω Πετράλωνα από Νεοναζί της Χρυσής Αυγής. Λίγες μέρες πριν τη δολοφονία του Παύλου είχε προηγηθεί δολοφονική επίθεση σε συνδικαλιστές του ΠΑΜΕ.


14 χρόνια από όταν η Χρυσή Αυγή μπήκε επίσημα ως κόμμα στην Ελληνική Βουλή το 2012, προσπαθώντας να κανονικοποιήσει με ρητορείες μίσους τις αυξανόμενες ρατσιστικές επιθέσεις σε μετανάστες, με αποκορύφωμα τη δολοφονική επίθεση σε Αιγύπτιους ψαράδες στο Πέραμα.


6 χρόνια από την καταδίκη της Χρυσής Αυγής 7/10/20 ως εγκληματική οργάνωση υπό τον μανδύα πολιτικού κόμματος, με τις προφυλακίσεις της ηγεσίας, του δολοφόνου του Παύλου Φύσσα, Γιώργου Ρουπακιά και αρκετών ακόμα μελών της.


6 μήνες από την τελεσίδικη καταδίκη της Νεοναζιστικής οργάνωσης σε δεύτερο βαθμό στο Εφετείο Αθηνών (Μάρτιος 2026).


Λίγες ημέρες πριν την αποφυλάκιση του Νεοναζί Χρυσαυγίτη Ηλία Κασιδιάρη μετά την έκτιση ποινής για διεύθυνση εγκληματικής οργάνωσης, ενώ έχουν αποφυλακιστεί ήδη ο αρχηγός της οργάνωσης Νίκος Μιχαλολιάκος από τον Σεπτέμβρη του 2025 και άλλα μέλη της νωρίτερα.


Στο σήμερα λοιπόν, έπειτα από 13 χρόνια ψυχοφθόρων υπερβάσεων εαυτών και γενναίων αγώνων του αντιφασιστικού κινήματος στους δρόμους και των αντιφασιστών δικηγόρων της πολιτικής αγωγής στα δικαστήρια, βρισκόμαστε σε περίοδο που ο φασιστικός εσμός επιχειρεί ξανά να βρει ιδεολογικό έδαφος σε κάθε κοινωνικό ζήτημα που προκαλεί τα κατώτερα ένστικτα της κοινής γνώμης, με ευτελείς αναλύσεις επάνω σε ψέματα και ιστορικές διαστρεβλώσεις.


Αυτό παράγει κάλπικη μόρφωση, που με απόλυτη βάση της και μόνο την ιδέα του έθνους, παράγει με τη σειρά της ένα κανιβαλικό αντιανθρώπινο μίσος:


Διαχωρίζει τους φτωχούς από τους μετανάστες φτωχούς, τους ντόπιους από τους πρόσφυγες, δαιμονοποιώντας τον εξαθλιωμένο αντί για αυτόν που τον εξαθλίωσε. Πρόκειται για τη διαχρονική προσπάθεια του φασισμού μέσα από τις οργανώσεις του να πείσει πως έρχεται ως αντισυστημική δύναμη επαναφοράς δικαιοσύνης, ενώ διατηρεί ξεκάθαρα υποτιμητική και εχθρική θέση απέναντι στους ταξικούς αγώνες των εργαζόμενων για δημόσια παιδεία, υγεία, εργασιακά δικαιώματα και τάσσεται με τις κατασταλτικές δυνάμεις απέναντι σε όσους και όσες αντιστέκονται σε πολιτικές ολοκληρωτισμού.


Λοιδορούν κάθε αγωνιστή ως παρακρατικό ενώ αποδεδειγμένα οι ίδιοι δρουν ως παρακρατικοί, ακριβώς όπως και οι πολιτικοί τους πρόγονοι, οι Χίτες και οι Ταγματασφαλίτες (αναμεσά τους και οι παππούδες του Ηλία Κασιδιάρη και πολλών άλλων μελών της Χ.Α) στον 2ο παγκόσμιο πόλεμο, οργανώσεις φιλοναζιστικές στο πλευρό των Γερμανών Ναζί, βασανιστές που κατέδιδαν τους αντάρτες που μάχονταν για την απελευθέρωση της χώρας, υποτακτικοί στις μεγάλες δυνάμεις που ανέκαθεν ορίζουν και διαμορφώνουν την αυτοκυριαρχία αυτού του τόπου κατά τα συμφέροντα της εκάστοτε οικονομικής αυτοκρατορίας.


Η άνοδος της ακροδεξιάς σε παγκόσμιο επίπεδο (όπως πχ στα πρώτα αποτελέσματα των φετινών γερμανικών εκλογών), αντιλαμβανόμαστε πως πατάει σε ένα σημαντικό κομμάτι της νεολαίας στις μέρες μας, το οποίο χρειάζεται απλώς να δει μια παρόμοια ενδυμασία με τη δικιά του, να ακούσει για παρανομίες και φυλακή, ώστε να θαυμάσει και να ακολουθήσει κάποιον, χωρίς να ενδιαφέρεται να ερευνήσει εις βάθος το υπόβαθρο, την πηγή της υποκίνησής του και το ιστορικό πλαίσιο γύρω του. Το εύκολο χρήμα και η εύπεπτη γνώση που κυνηγούν οι νέοι σε περίοδο εκτεταμένης ακρίβειας, μεταφράζεται συχνά και σε εύπεπτη πολιτική κατήχηση.


Από την πλευρά μας, έχουμε το χρέος που μας άφησαν οι άδικα σκοτωμένοι από φασιστικά χέρια, να καλούμε ξανά και ξανά κάθε νεό άνθρωπο, όχι να συνταχθεί πλήρως με εμάς, αλλά πρώτα και κύρια και αναζητήσει την αντικειμενική ιστορική πραγματικότητα, να διαβάσει, να ρωτήσει για τα γεγονότα που διαμόρφωσαν την ιστορία της γειτονιάς του, να βγει στο δρόμο απέναντι στις κεφαλαιοκρατικές θανατοπολιτικές που φτωχοποιούν εκείνον και την οικογένειά του, να διαπιστώσει ποιοι βρίσκονται ήδη εκεί να κινητοποιούνται και γιατί.


Να μην αναθέτει τη δράση του σε κανέναν τρίτο αλλά να γνωρίσει την αξία της συμμετοχής στα κοινά, με τις εντάσεις, τους ενθουσιασμούς, τις απογοητεύσεις, τις συντροφιές, τις συγκρούσεις και τις λυτρώσεις που αυτή φέρει.


Να ψάξει την ιστορία …

author: Shahad Ali
title: Gazans Feel Despair as Israeli Officials Cement Plans for Permanent Occupation
content:
Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has described a plan to remove Palestinians from the Gaza Strip to other countries.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Nearly a year after Donald Trump announced the creation of the “Board of Peace,” which was ostensibly charged with ending Israel’s genocidal assault on Gaza and overseeing reconstruction, one of the figures most centrally involved in the body has warned that a complete collapse of the so-called ceasefire in Gaza could lead to a “point of no return.”

Nickolay Mladenov, the Bulgarian diplomat who serves as Gaza’s High Representative on the Board of Peace, made the comments during a UN Security Council session on Wednesday, August 26. Casualty numbers in Gaza have dropped, he noted, but have not ceased, offering a pointed critique of Israel’s continued bombardment despite the supposed cessation of hostilities.

“If this ceasefire collapses and the strip spirals into another full escalation, there will be no road map to return to, there will be no administration to deploy, and there will be nothing left on the ground to rebuild,” he said.

In his remarks, Mladenov also noted that Hamas and armed factions in the Gaza Strip had agreed to disarm and transfer civilian and security responsibilities to a transitional authority recognized by the United Nations. This was the first time Hamas and the armed factions within Gaza had agreed to such a step, Mladenov announced, which is part of a plan for a new phase of the ceasefire in Gaza. The road map also includes the dismantling of all weapons in the Strip and its demilitarization, subject to verification and monitoring; the complete transfer of civilian and security governance in Gaza; the reconstruction of destroyed areas so people can return to normal life; and a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Gaza tied to progress in disarmament.

The full implementation of this 15-point comprehensive plan, which Mladenov had outlined to the council earlier this year, would provide an opportunity to “dramatically improve the lives of Palestinians in Gaza in a sustainable way, provide durable security for Israelis, and move from a conflict that has destabilized the region toward an environment that provides peace, prosperity and economic opportunities for the entire Middle East.”

These comments spread rapidly across Gaza. In displacement camps, Gazans gathered to discuss the details of the road map and the extent to which it might improve the horrific conditions they endure in overcrowded and flimsy tents, deprived of even the basic necessities of life. More than 2 million Palestinians concentrated in only around 30 percent of the Gaza Strip have been left so desperate that we scan news headlines for any indication of a possible end to our suffering. For many, the renewed interest in the Board of Peace plan became a lifeline they could cling to — hoping for a chance to live in peace, rebuild their destroyed lives, and return to areas now controlled by Israel beyond the so-called “Yellow Line.”

“We are living a life deprived of any stability or even a sense of safety. We have literally reached a point where we think about death every minute and go to sleep without knowing what might happen tomorrow.”

However, Mladenov’s announcement has been met with statements from Israeli officials that contradict the Board of Peace’s vision for Gaza’s future and reflect their unwillingness to withdraw from areas under Israeli control.

Before Mladenov’s address, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu had already said he would reject the plan, despite the road map’s connection to U.S. President Donald Trump. During a September 2 visit to Israeli forces in the Gaza Strip, Netanyahu also said he had no plans to withdraw from territory under Israeli control. “We are not withdrawing. We are staying along this line, and we control more than 60 percent of the Strip, and there is more still to come,” he said, stressing that military operations against those he described as threatening Israel’s security would continue.

Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz also confirmed in a statement on September 1 that Israeli troops would remain inside the Gaza Strip even after Hamas is disarmed and Gaza is demilitarized. author: Adam Mahoney
title: The EPA Is Planning to Scrap Public Review Rules for Data Center Pollution
content:
Americans strongly oppose data centers in their communities. The federal government wants to make them easier to build.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Americans don’t agree on much, but that’s not the case when it comes to data centers.

​Seven in 10 Americans oppose building data centers for artificial intelligence in or near their communities. Despite this, the federal government is moving to make it easier for them to be built. And in some places, residents won’t even get the chance to raise concerns publicly or even know if a data center is coming to their neighborhoods.

The federal Environmental Protection Agency plans to scrap a federal requirement that states tell the public — and allow public comment — before approving air-pollution permits for industrial facilities. That includes the data centers rising across the country, as well as the power plants built to feed their enormous appetite for electricity.

At the same time, the EPA last month also proposed another change that would let developers start building data centers before their permits are approved.

The rural South, which is home to a disproportionate amount of Black communities, has seen the largest growth of these large data centers. The proposals and lack of transparency may worsen health risks, increase utility bills, and contribute to community displacement, residents told Capital B.

​The change at the federal level would mean that, in some places, residents could lose one of their few formal chances to ask questions, raise alarms, or learn that a data center is headed their way before the permits are signed and construction begins.

Paul Black, an environmental activist organizing against a data center complex the size of 1,200 football fields in rural South Carolina, said these moves “run counter to the way American democracy is sold to us.”

“It is a betrayal of everything that this country should stand for, purports to stand for. It runs counter to the will of the people,” he added.

The data center project currently being debated in his 40% Black community was only proposed there after developers tried — and failed — to build a similar campus in a predominantly white county in Georgia.​

​The change at the federal level would mean that, in some places, residents could lose one of their few formal chances to ask questions, raise alarms, or learn that a data center is headed their way before the permits are signed and construction begins.

In a statement, the EPA said the proposal would “provide the state and local agencies most familiar with local issues the discretion to determine whether, when, and for how long to provide opportunities for public participation.”

But many Americans are increasingly losing faith in their local governments to work in their best interests.

In part of a growing web of secrecy, local governments have routinely signed nondisclosure agreements with tech companies to hide these projects and overruled legal orders in order to bury information about them.

“What I am saying is that if we, as the community, the people who are responsible, can’t understand this, can’t have questions answered, can’t have information, then how can I look somebody in the eye and tell them this is good for you, trust me?” Davante Lewis, a Louisiana public service commissioner tasked with regulating industry, told Capital B last month.

Lewis was the only member to vote in favor of releasing electricity use information tied to the current construction of the country’s largest data center in rural Louisiana.

Nearly 200 advocacy groups and more than a dozen states, led by both Democrats and Republicans, have voiced opposition to the federal changes.

​“In the more rural parts of the nation, we are under attack by data centers,” Black said. “They are seeking to get in as fast as possible, as quietly as possible, and do what they will to the places [where] we live, that we find precious, the places that we’ve preserved, and they want to come in in the dark of the night to build a data center.”

Last month, South Carolina passed its own ruling that says power plants for data centers can be constructed without review or approval from the state’s regulatory commission.

author: Ariana Figueroa
title: New Lawsuit Is Challenging Trump Admin Plan to Allow ICE at Polling Places
content:
“The specter of armed officers at polling places threatens the freedom of this upcoming election,” the lawsuit says.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Washington — Latino advocacy groups and voting rights organizations Thursday filed a suit in federal court challenging the Trump administration’s policy of allowing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers to enter polling locations in certain circumstances to conduct immigration enforcement during the 2026 midterm elections.

The suit in the District Court for the District of Columbia argues that Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s recent comments that ICE agents would be at polling locations for the purpose of immigration enforcement violates federal law that prohibits federal “armed men” at election sites.

The statute allows for “troops” or “armed men” at polling locations only if “such force be necessary to repel armed enemies of the United States.”

“The specter of armed officers at polling places threatens the freedom of this upcoming election,” according to the lawsuit. “It places voters in fear that they will be confronted by armed federal immigration enforcement officers if they choose to cast a ballot.”

In a statement to States Newsroom, a DHS spokesperson said that “ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations.”

“ICE conducts intelligence-driven targeted enforcement, and if an active public safety threat endangered a polling location, they may be arrested as a result of that targeted enforcement action,” the spokesperson said.

Earlier this month, Mullin said that ICE officers at polling locations would be there “to enforce specific threats.”

“The only reason why we would be at polling places, if there is a threat to that polling place or we’re serving a warrant on someone that we have been actively tracking down,” he said. “ICE’s job is immigration (and) custom enforcement. That’s their job and so if we’re doing something, we’re doing that specifically.”

The suit asks the federal court to prevent the Trump administration from following that polling place policy and declaring it unlawful, as well as barring “officers from operating or carrying weapons in the vicinity of open polling places, including dropboxes, curbside voting locations, and similar places where votes are taken, collected, received, counted, or certified during early voting periods and on Election Day itself, for any reason other than repelling armed enemies of the United States.”

The civil rights groups that joined the suit said the tactic would lead to voter suppression.

“Sending armed ICE officers to polling places is not immigration enforcement — it is voter suppression, plain and simple,” UnidosUS President Janet Murguía said in a statement. “All Americans — including Latino voters — have a constitutional right to cast their ballot without fear of interrogation, detention, or family separation.”

The suit was filed by the oldest U.S. Latino civil rights organization, League of United Latin American Citizens, or LULAC; the largest Hispanic civil rights organization, UnidosUS; the voter mobilization group Common Cause; and the city and county of Denver, Colorado, which has a large immigrant population and has been targeted by ICE multiple times for immigration enforcement.

“The right to vote, and to do so without fear of intimidation, is fundamental to our democracy and to being an American,” Denver Mayor Mike Johnston said in a statement. “Stationing ICE agents near polling places is only meant to scare people and suppress votes. We’ll fight tooth and nail to prevent it.”

title: Valilikten belediyeye 'Rojbash' yazısı: "Gösterim fiilen engellendi"
content:
Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediyesi, yaz boyunca Sümerpark Amfi Tiyatrosu’nda düzenlediği açık hava sineması etkinlikleri kapsamında filmi 13 Eylül akşamı ücretsiz olarak seyirciyle buluşturmak istedi.


Diyarbakır İl Emniyet Müdürlüğü ise 9 Eylül tarihli yazısında, Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı’nın

Rojbash

 hakkında 7 Ağustos 2024’te verdiği “ticari dolaşıma ve gösterime sunulmasının uygun bulunmadığı” yönündeki kararın halen yürürlükte olduğunu hatırlattı ve planlanan gösterimin İl Kültür ve Turizm Müdürlüğü ile Diyarbakır Büyükşehir Belediyesi tarafından “tekrar değerlendirilmesini” istedi.


Yazı doğrudan bir gösterim yasağı kararı içermiyor. Ancak gelişmeyi bianet’e değerlendiren yönetmen Özkan Küçük’e göre sonuç fiilen aynı oldu: Daha önce festivallerde ve özel etkinliklerde ücretsiz gösterilebilen film, bu kez perdeye çıkamadı.


Doğrusu ilk defa fiili olarak gösterimin yapılmasını engellemeye dönük bir şeyle karşılaştık. Film daha önce İstanbul ve Diyarbakır’daki festivallerde gösterildi, birkaç özel gösterim de yaptık. Bunların hepsi ücretsizdi ve biz bunların Bakanlığın kararına aykırı olmadığını düşünüyorduk. Bu kez belediyenin duyurusunun ardından Emniyet’in yazısı geldi. Avukatlarımızla değerlendirdik. Normalde ticari bir gösterim olmadığı için buna hakkımız olduğunu düşünüyoruz ama istinaf kararı bizim aleyhimize daha farklı bir durum yarattı. Hem olası bir cezayı hem de belediyenin zor durumda kalmasını göze almak istemedik. Sonuçta ilk defa film fiilen engellenmiş oldu.


Bir sınıflandırma başvurusu nasıl yasağa dönüştü?


Rojbash

’ın idareyle karşılaşması 2024’te başladı.


Küçük ve ekibi filmi vizyona sokabilmek için Mayıs 2024’te Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı’na tescil ve sınıflandırma başvurusu yaptı. Küçük’ün anlattığına göre, normalde filme yaş sınırlaması gibi işaretlerin verilmesiyle sonuçlanan süreç

Rojbash

 için farklı işledi.


Bakanlık filmi “ticari dolaşıma ve gösterime uygun” bulmadı.


Film ekibi kararı yargıya taşıdı. Ankara 3. İdare Mahkemesi Bakanlığın işlemini hukuka uygun bulmayarak kaldırdı. Ancak Bakanlık kararı istinafa götürdü. Bölge İdare Mahkemesi de ilk derece mahkemesinin kararını kaldırarak Bakanlığın işlemini hukuka uygun buldu. Dava şimdi Danıştay’da sürüyor.


Küçük, bu süreç boyunca kararın lafzındaki “ticari” ibaresini esas aldıklarını ve ücretsiz festival ile özel gösterimlerin kapsam dışında olduğunu düşündüklerini söylüyor. Bu nedenle filmi +18 ibaresiyle çeşitli ücretsiz etkinliklerde göstermeyi sürdürdüler.


Sümerpark gösteriminin yapılamaması ise Küçük’e göre bu alanın da kapanabileceğini gösteriyor:


Bugüne kadar vizyona giremedik ama en azından festivallerde ve özel gösterimlerde seyirciyle buluşabiliyorduk. Şimdi bu artık onları da yapamayacağımız anlamına geliyor. Muhtemelen yapsak ileride bir cezayla karşı karşıya kalabilirdik. Bu da dava sonuçlanana kadar böyle bir girişimde bulunamayacağımız bir noktaya götürüyor bizi. Çözümsüz bir yere.


Yasakları anlatan filmin kendi yasağı


Rojbash

, yaklaşık 30 yıl önce oynadıkları bir oyunu yeniden sahnelemek üzere bir araya gelen Kürt tiyatrocuları anlatıyor. Filmin anlattığı hikâyeyle bugün başına gelenler arasındaki mesafe ise giderek kapanıyor.


Geçmiş dönemdeki yasaklarla bugün hâlâ süren yasaklar arasında bir git-gel var filmde. Bazı olumsuz engellerin tekrar başa sarması üzerine ironik bir hikâye anlatıyoruz. Ama bunu anlatan filmin de yasaklanmış olması, üstelik demokratikleşme, silahsızlanma ve barışın konuşulduğu bir dönemde bu yasağın sürüyor olması çok tuhaf. Buralardan başlamaz mı acaba bu barış, demokratikleşme ya da Kürtlerin haklarıyla ilgili adımlar? Böyle şeyler biraz değişse belki toplum da bu olasılıklara daha fazla inanabilir.


Küçük, Bakanlığın ilk kararı verildiğinde bugünkü siyasal sürecin başlamadığını, ancak dava sürerken koşulların değiştiğini hatırlatıyor. Buna rağmen Bakanlık avukatlarının ilk derece mahkemesinde kaybettikleri davayı istinafa taşımasını ve yasağın sürmesindeki ısrarı eleştiriyor.


“Milletvekillerinin gündemine bile girmedi”


Küçük’ün eleştirisi yalnızca idari ve yargısal makamlara yönelik değil.

Rojbash

 hakkındaki yasağın kamuoyunda ve siyasette yeterince karşılık bulmadığını düşünüyor.

title: Palestinian Unions: Global Call for Worker Action Against Genocide this November
content:
https://www.instagram.com/p/DdJQXHgDh1I

Palestinian Unions: Global Call for Worker Action Against Genocide this November

Author info Palestinian Trade Unions

The Palestinian labor movement reiterates its solidarity with workers across the world resisting all forms of oppression and calls for global action to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing genocide and apartheid from Friday, November 20th leading up to the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People on Sunday, November 29th 2026.

This coming November, we the undersigned Palestinian trade unions and federations urgently renew our call to unions around the world to:

Uphold and defend the inalienable rights of the Indigenous people of Palestine as stipulated in international law, particularly the right of our refugees to return home and receive reparations, and

Escalate BDS pressure to end all state, corporate and institutional complicity in Israel’s illegal occupation, apartheid and genocide.

While approaching the third anniversary of the beginning of Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and the International Day of Solidarity with the Palestinian People, and in light of Israel’s accelerating ethnic cleansing, annexation, settler violence and pogroms in the West Bank, and depraved violent repression of our prisoners, we remind ourselves that an injury to one is an injury to all. Israel’s livestreamed genocide, coupled with the wars and threats of aggression by its imperialist partners in Washington, is leading to the collapse of respect for international law, human rights and workers’ rights, threatening humanity at large, not just Palestinians.

Today, the Palestinian struggle for justice is at the heart of the battle against a world order of “might makes right” that is being imposed by the U.S-Israel genocidal axis and enabled by colonial powers. As Israel’s wars of aggression against the peoples of the region expand from Lebanon to Syria and from Yemen to Iran, and as the US threatens the peoples of Cuba, Greenland, Venezuela, Oman, among others, it is clear that hardly anyone is safe from this descent to the abyss.

The Israel-US axis is waging its war for Greater Israel without any consideration for the global recession (maybe even depression) it is potentially creating and its impacts globally. This includes the exacerbation of the cost of living crisis, austerity measures, the housing crisis, food insecurity, among others. Military budgets are swelling at the cost of health, housing and education. The first to feel the brunt of all this are working people and their families. The demands for affordability, fair wages, more and better social services, and lower living costs are organically connected to the calls for an end to astronomical military spending, vicious privatisation, and global complicity in Israeli crimes. This affects us all and therefore should unite us all. Where states fail to uphold international law and end their own complicity, workers and their unions must take the lead in acting to end this complicity!

Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.

It is the duty of unions to ensure that the workers they represent—whether in ports, on ships, in businesses, or in government offices—are not involved, often without their knowledge and/or consent, in actions that involve complicity in atrocity crimes anywhere, including Israel’s war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide against our people.

The 2024 decisions of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) – that Israel is plausibly committing genocide, that its occupation is illegal, and its policies amount to apartheid – make ending all complicity in Israel’s crimes not only a moral but also a legal obligation. States, institutions (including unions) and corporations must impose targeted, lawful sanctions on Israel. We call on all union bodies and civil society organisations worldwide to organise, uplift and turn solidarity into concrete strategic action across the ten days leading up to the international day of solidarity with the Palestinian people from November 20th to November 29th 2026.

author: Maha Hilal
title: 25 Years Later, We Still Live in the World the War on Terror Made
content:
The war on terror was not inevitable, nor was the extraordinary violence carried out in its name necessary.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

In a 2013 Congressional hearing on drone warfare, a young Pakistani boy named Zubair Rehman, aged 13 at the time, talked about the feeling of living under the threat of constant drone strikes. In his powerful testimony, Zubair stated that “I no longer love blue skies. In fact, I now prefer gray skies…The drones do not fly when the skies are gray…When the sky brightens, drones return and we live in fear.”

More than a decade after his testimony and twenty-five years into the so-called global war on terror, far from being a relic of the past, drone warfare is one of the many omnipresent threats that have been cemented by the U.S. in countries across the globe. Generations of Muslim children have grown up in the world that the war on terror has created — a world in which endless war has been normalized, torture justified, and with both the state and the media painting a target on the backs on entire Muslim populations across the globe. For children like Zubair, who should be turning 26 this year, the color of the sky still serves as an ominous threat warning of the likelihood of state violence.

Within the United States, much of the media coverage of the September 11 attacks has focused on assessments of the war on terror and retrospective lessons. Of course, what goes largely undercovered are some of the injustices that followed in its wake, such as the Islamophobia directed at Muslims and bigotry against other racialized populations within the U.S. Mainstream media has also largely minimized the extent to which the war on terror has fundamentally reshaped political and social life within the United States. Islamophobia has been central to this transformation, permeating political discourse and providing the ideological justification for increasingly repressive policies. Even though much of the war on terror has been shrouded in secrecy, many forms of its violence and horrors have been transformed into spectacles of violence in order to normalize the punishment of Muslims while rendering Muslim life disposable, all in the service of preserving an enduring national security apparatus.

At the twenty-five-year juncture of the war on terror, we know now more than ever that the way this war has been fought was not inevitable, nor was the extraordinary violence carried out in its name necessary. We also know that the war on terror was never about ending political violence, but instead about building a sustained campaign and continuum of violence that has included large-scale wars like the invasions and occupations of Afghanistan and Iraq; the continuous bombing of Yemen, Somalia, Pakistan, and now Iran; mass surveillance; and indefinite detention and torture, among numerous other injustices. The “forever wars,” as those in Afghanistan and Iraq are often labelled, imply that they are never-ending because of the lack of a plan. But if we have learned anything about U.S. wars, it’s that they never really end and instead only morph into violence that preserves the brutality of past wars. Moreover, U.S. imperialism never emerges as an unintended consequence; it is always by design.

Two and a half decades after the war on terror was launched and with devastating state violence that has continued to evolve and expand, we know that this war was never meant to end.

That’s why we must renew our commitment to confronting the war on terror and the totality of its violence — its wars, institutions, laws, technologies, and narratives — in order to dismantle the apparatus it has entrenched, and secure meaningful accountability and justice for the millions of people whose lives have been devastated in the name of national security.

In a speech to a Joint Session of Congress on September 20th, 2001, just nine days after the September 11th attacks, President George W. Bush officially declared the launch of the war on terror. Laying out the official narrative of the war, including identifying the perpetrators of the attacks and their motivations for attacking the United States, he advised the American public that they “should not expect one battle, but a lengthy campaign, unlike any other we have ever seen.”

“Our war on terror begins with al Qaeda, but it does not end there,” Bush proclaimed. “It will not end until …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Oil Prices Soar to New Heights as Houthis Seize Yemen’s Red Sea Coastline
content:
A top economist estimated that Trump’s Iran war has already cost the average American household an extra $1,650.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Houthi forces have reportedly seized the entirety of Yemen’s Red Sea coastline, further solidifying the group’s control over its key waterway and sending oil prices soaring to even further heights since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran.

The Houthis, also known as Ansar Allah, seized control of the key port town of Mocha this week, reports say. They have since rapidly advanced to controlling the entire Red Sea coast, and, on Friday, reached the strategic island of Perim, which sits in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

This gives the Iran-backed rebel group even further control over Bab al-Mandeb, which is one of the world’s most critical shipping routes, with about 12 percent of global seaborne-traded oil typically passing through the strait.

This is the latest escalation in its decade-long fight against the Saudi Arabia-backed Yemeni forces, which has flared up in recent months amid the war on Iran. Over a thousand people have been killed or wounded in the past two weeks of fighting in southwest Yemen, aid agencies have reported, while tens of thousands have been displaced.

Satellite images on Thursday also showed a large amount of black smoke rising from an area of Saudi Arabia’s crucial East-West oil pipeline, which has been critical for the petrostate for diverting oil exports amid the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

In July, Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabian ships passing through Bab al-Mandeb, a response to Saudi strikes on Sanaa International Airport earlier that month and the country’s years-long blockade on Yemen.

But the Houthis have also threatened to close or slow traffic through the strait for years, in response to Israel’s genocide in Gaza and, then, the U.S.’s attacks on Yemen under President Joe Biden. In July, Iranian officials reportedly also asked the Houthis to close Bab al-Mandeb if the U.S. progressed its strikes on Iranian civilian infrastructure, as President Donald Trump repeatedly threatened to do.

The U.S. is providing Saudi Arabia with intelligence and support as it fights the Houthis. But Trump has reportedly declined Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s request for the U.S. to directly launch strikes against the Houthis, Axios reported on Friday — though war hawks on both sides of the aisle have urged the Trump administration to back the fighting more directly. The U.S. also killed over 150 Yemeni civilians in Trump’s targeting of Houthis last year, a fact that the Pentagon belatedly admitted months later.

Meanwhile, the fighting and threats to the strait, in combination with the pressures caused by the war on Iran, sent oil prices to $110 a barrel on Friday. Diesel prices hit a record high in the U.S., rising above $6 per gallon on average. On Thursday, several gas stations in California maxed out their values for diesel at $9.999 a gallon — the highest number the pumps can display.

This will translate to an even worse affordability crunch in the U.S. in relation to the U.S.’s war on Iran, which has already cost over $100 billion just in additional gas prices. In combination with other factors like rising energy costs and interest rates, Moody’s Analytics’s top economist estimated on Thursday that the war has cost the average American household $1,650 already — with no end in sight to Middle East wars.

title: People of Maxmur commemorate the martyrs of the freedom struggle
content:
A commemoration for those who lost their lives in the Kurdish freedom struggle was held at the self-administered Şehîd Rûstem Cudî refugee camp in Maxmur, Southern Kurdistan. Numerous residents gathered at the institution representing the families of the martyrs.


After the names and biographies of Avesta Fîraz Herekol, Îsmaîl, Ronahî Bilikî, Botan Çiyayî, Zerîn Şoreş, Têkoşer Mehmed, Rojbîn Asya, Çekdar Cudî, Elî Çîçek, Bêrîtan Rûken, Hacer Hîlal, Çiya Vîetnam Cûdî, Mizgîn Tetwan, Birûsk Amed, Çekdar Melek, Tekîn Hemzo Harûn, Rojhat, Evîn Feraşîn, Aras Piling Goyî, Rojda Fîkret, Qehreman Botan, Zinar Osyan and Andok Cîhan were read out, Bedran Pîranî, Co-Chair of the Maxmur People’s Council, addressed the gathering. He recalled the heavy sacrifices made in the struggle for a free life in Kurdistan.


“In order to live freely on our own land, we have had to pay a heavy price. The price of freedom is very high,” Pîranî said. Those we commemorate here today lost their lives at different times and in different places, but all had left their mark on history. They are all children of this people.”


“No one can deny the Kurdish people anymore”


Pîranî pointed in particular to the changes that decades of struggle for freedom have brought about in how Kurds are perceived. “A people whose very existence was once not even recognized is now known around the world. No one can deny the Kurdish people anymore. If we are recognized today and can express ourselves freely, we owe it to our martyrs,” Pîranî said.


Relatives of the martyrs also addressed the gathering. They reaffirmed their commitment to preserving the memory of the martyrs and continuing their struggle. Following the commemoration, condolences were received at the center of the Committee of Families of the Martyrs.

author: Unknown
title: Repression against women in Iran continues
content:
The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) highlighted the ongoing repression of women by the Iranian state in a report it published.


It was reported that Seba Sedifi, a member of the Baha’i faith who was detained by security forces yesterday outside her home in Tehran, was first taken to the Jenatabad Prosecutor’s Office to begin serving her finalized three-year-and-five-month prison sentence, and was then transferred to Qarchak Prison in Varamin to serve her sentence.


Seba Sedifi was also detained in January 2022. She was taken to Branch 2 of the Evin Prosecutor’s Office and was released approximately one and a half months later on bail of 1.5 billion tomans.


Meanwhile, it was announced that Perîsa Kemali Merdikani, a political prisoner and geography student who suffers from a serious intestinal and digestive illness, had been sentenced to 11 years in prison and two years of exile. Perisa Kemalî Merdikanî was transferred from Yazd Prison to Bandar Abbas Prison without prior notice.


Mutehere Gonabadi, a former member of the Tehran University Council who had previously been sentenced to 21 months in prison on charges of “propaganda against the system,” was also reportedly transferred from Qarchak Prison to Evin Prison.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Justicia realpolitik
content:
En las últimas semanas el presidente Javier Milei y el ministro de Justicia Juan B. Mahiques firmaron las 

designaciones

 de más sesenta jueces, defensores y fiscales, cuyos pliegos obtuvieron el acuerdo de una abrumadora y transversal mayoría de senadores y senadoras, incluso aquellos que habían sido denunciados por turbios vínculos con poderes económicos y servicios de inteligencia.


Jura de Pablo Bertuzzi y Pablo Yadarola como camaristas federales en Comodoro Py el 3 de septiembre de 2026.


Por Paula Litvachky


En el ámbito de las decisiones judiciales, en los primeros días de septiembre, Gustavo Arribas, Silvia Majdalani y otros ex funcionarios de la agencia de Inteligencia (ahora Side, antes AFI),

fueron sobreseídos

 en un caso que debía investigar el perfilamiento ilegal de periodistas y militantes políticos, en el contexto de las reuniones del G20 y de la OMC en nuestro país.


Lo mismo sucedió en 2025, en

la causa por el espionaje contra las familias

 de los tripulantes del submarino Ara San Juan, y a mediados de 2026 con la investigación del llamado “proyecto AMBA”.


La causa contra la banda de los agentes orgánicos e inorgánicos “Super Mario Bros” quedó totalmente desmembrada y sigue abierta para juzgarlos como si fueran cuentapropistas.


Aunque en todos estos hechos hay fuertes indicios de prácticas de inteligencia ilegal planificada, que amenazan el ejercicio de derechos y la disidencia política, el Poder Judicial optó por clausurar las investigaciones. Además del efecto de estas decisiones en cada caso concreto, el encadenamiento de sobreseimientos va construyendo una jurisprudencia contraria a la posibilidad de que se condenen prácticas estatales de inteligencia política que están prohibidas.


Juan Bautista Mahiques en su asunción como ministro de Justicia de Javier Milei


Cuatro años después de que saliera a la luz el encuentro de Lago Escondido, uno de los participantes de aquel viaje es ahora ministro de Justicia y otro obtuvo el acuerdo para integrar la Cámara Federal. Y Carlos Mahiques, padre del ministro y también asistente al viaje, fue autorizado a permanecer en la Cámara de Casación Federal en la que no está designado. Aquellos días en los que la denuncia estuvo en el centro de la conversación pública fueron arrasados por decisiones que se buscan justificar en la realpolitik.


Felices los 4


En las puntas, los nuevos camaristas federales Pablo Bertuzzi (izquierda) y Pablo Yadarola (derecha)


Hacia adentro, Mariano Llorens y Carlos “Coco” Mahiques, los jefes del lawfare en Comodoro Py.

pic.twitter.com/k0pVJ2a20u


— ari lijalad (@arilijalad)

September 3, 2026


Sin embargo, estas escenas expresan algo más de fondo: la idea de que no conviene o no es viable confrontar con ese sector del Poder Judicial que se consolida victorioso en el esquema político y de negocios actual.


Parece terminar un ciclo de confrontación que merece todavía un balance político, sobre sus posibilidades, límites y errores, pero eso no puede significar una aceptación total, y de algún modo cómplice, con un estado de cosas, con un sistema judicial que abandona su función de protección de derechos.


Paula Litvachky es Directora ejecutiva del CELS Columna publicada en la edición de septiembre de Posdata, el boletín del CELS.
